text: You may...
options: Drive your vehicle on the sidewalk at night.
Reverse your vehicle only if it is safe to do so.
Leave the engine of your vehicle idling when you put petrol in it.
explanation: You may only reverse your vehicle if it is safe to do so. Reversing unsafely can endanger pedestrians or other vehicles.

text:
When you want to change lanes and drive from one lane to the other you must:
(i) Only do it when it is safe to do so
(ii) Switch on your flickers in time to show what you are going to do
(iii) Use the mirrors of your vehicle to ensure that you know of other traffic around you
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct
All of the above are correct
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct
explanation: All three actions are required when changing lanes — check for safety, signal your intention, and use your mirrors to stay aware of other traffic.

text:
When may you not overtake another vehicle? When you:
(i) Are nearing the top of a hill
(ii) Are nearing a curve
(iii) Can only see 100m in front of you because of dust over the road
options: (i) only is correct
All of the above is correct
(i) and (ii) only are correct
explanation: You may not overtake when your view of the road ahead is restricted — such as near the top of a hill, around a curve, or when visibility is poor due to dust or other obstructions. All of these situations are unsafe for overtaking.

text:
When are you allowed to drive on the shoulder of a road?
(i) Any time if you want to let another vehicle pass you
(ii) In daytime when you want to allow another vehicle to pass you and it is safe
(iii) When on a freeway with 4 lanes in both directions, you want to drive slower than 120 km/h
(iv) When you have a flat tyre and you want to park there to change it
options: (i), (iii) and (iv) only are correct
(ii) and (iv) only are correct
All of the above are correct
explanation: You may drive on the shoulder only during the day to let another vehicle pass when it is safe, or to stop in an emergency such as changing a flat tyre.

text:
You may not obtain a learner's licence if:
(i) You already have a licence that authorises the driving of the same vehicle class.
(ii) You are declared unfit to obtain a driving licence for a certain period and that period still prevails.
(iii) Your licence was suspended temporarily and the suspension has not yet expired.
options: (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct
(i) only is correct
(i) and (iii)
explanation: You may not obtain a learner's licence if you already hold a licence for that class, are declared unfit to obtain a licence, or your current licence is still under suspension.

text: At an intersection...
options: Vehicles have the right of way over pedestrians.
You must yield to oncoming traffic if you want to turn right.
You can use a stop sign as a yield sign if there is no other traffic.
explanation: When turning right at an intersection, you must yield to oncoming traffic to avoid collisions. Vehicles coming straight through the intersection have the right of way.

text: The licence for your vehicle (clearance certificate) is valid for...
options: 12 months
90 days
21 days
explanation: A vehicle licence, also known as a clearance certificate, is valid for 12 months from the date of issue before it must be renewed.

text: Unless otherwise shown by a sign, the general speed limit in an urban area is... km/h.
explanation: In South Africa, the general speed limit in urban areas is 60 km/h unless a different limit is indicated by a road sign.

text: The legal speed limit which you may drive...
options: Is always 120 km/h outside an urban area
Can be determined by yourself if you look at the number of lanes the road has
Is shown to you by signs next to the road
explanation: The legal speed limit is indicated by regulatory road signs displayed along the road. Drivers must always obey the posted speed limit signs.

text: You may...
options: Leave your vehicle's engine running without supervision
Allow someone to ride on the bumper of your vehicle
Put your arm out of the window only to give legal hand signals
explanation: You may only put your arm out of the window to make legal hand signals when required. Doing so for any other reason is not permitted.

text:
If you see that someone wants to overtake you, you must:
(i) Not drive faster
(ii) Keep to the left as far as is safe
(iii) Give hand signals to allow the person to pass safely
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct
All of the above are correct
(ii) is only correct
explanation: When another vehicle wants to overtake, you must not increase your speed and should keep as far left as is safe to let them pass. Hand signals are not required in this situation.

text: What is the longest period that a vehicle may be parked on one place on a road outside urban areas?
options: 7 days
48 hours
24 hours
explanation: A vehicle may not be parked in one place on a public road outside an urban area for longer than 24 hours.

text: At an intersection...
options: You can pass another vehicle waiting to turn right on his left side by going off the road
You can stop in it to offload passengers
Pedestrians who are already crossing the road when the red man signal starts showing have right of way
explanation: Pedestrians who are already crossing the road when the red man signal appears have the right of way and must be allowed to finish crossing safely.

text: You are not allowed to stop...
options: On the pavement
With the front of your vehicle facing oncoming traffic
Next to any obstruction in the road
explanation: You may not stop with the front of your vehicle facing oncoming traffic, as it creates a hazard and confusion for other road users.

text: You are not allowed to stop...
options: Where you are also prohibited to park
5 m from a bridge
Opposite a vehicle, where the roadway is 10 m wide
explanation: You are not allowed to stop within 5 metres of a bridge as it may obstruct visibility or create a traffic hazard.

text:
You may pass another vehicle on the left-hand side if it:
(i) Indicates that it is going to turn right
(ii) Drives on the right-hand side of a road with a shoulder where you can pass
(iii) Drives in a town in the right-hand lane with 2 lanes in the same direction
options: (i) and (iii) only are correct
All of the above are correct
(i) only is correct
explanation: You may pass on the left only if the vehicle ahead has signaled to turn right, or if there are two or more lanes going in the same direction within a town.

text:
You may overtake another vehicle on the left-hand side:
(i) When that vehicle is going to turn right and the road is wide enough that it is not necessary to drive on the shoulder
(ii) Where the road has 2 lanes for traffic in the same direction
(iii) If a police officer instructs you to do so
options: (iii) only is correct
(ii) and (iii) only are correct
All of the above are correct
explanation: You may overtake on the left if the vehicle ahead is turning right, where there are two lanes in the same direction, or when instructed by a police officer.

text: You may on a public road...
options: Pass another vehicle turning right, on its left-hand side without driving on the shoulder of the road
Pass another vehicle at any place on the left-hand side if it is turning right
Not pass any vehicle on the left-hand side
explanation: You may pass another vehicle on the left-hand side only if it is turning right and there is enough space to do so safely without driving on the shoulder.

text: The last action that you must take before moving to another lane is to...
options: Switch on your flicker
Check the blind spot
Look in rear view mirror
explanation: Before changing lanes, the final step is to check your blind spot to ensure there are no vehicles or cyclists beside you that are not visible in your mirrors.

text: When are you allowed to drive your vehicle on the right-hand side of a road with traffic in both directions?
options: When you switch the emergency lights of your vehicle on
When a traffic officer shows you to do so
Under no circumstances
explanation: You may only drive on the right-hand side of a two-way road if instructed by a traffic officer. Doing so otherwise is illegal and unsafe.

text: If you come to a robot and the red light flashes, you must...
options: Stop and wait for the light to change to green before you go
Stop and go only if it is safe to do so
Look out for a road block as the light shows you a police stop
explanation: A flashing red traffic light means you must stop completely and proceed only when it is safe to do so, treating it like a stop sign.

text: A vehicle of which the brakes are not good, must be towed...
options: With a rope
With a tow-bar
On a trailer
explanation: If a vehicle’s brakes are faulty, it must be towed using a tow-bar to maintain control and safety between the vehicles.

text: A safe following distance is, when the vehicle in front of you suddenly stops, you could...
options: Stop without swerving
Swerve and stop next to it
Swerve and pass
explanation: A safe following distance allows you to stop safely and in time without swerving or colliding with the vehicle in front of you.

text: You may not...
options: Have passengers in the vehicle if you only have a learner's licence
Leave your vehicle unattended while the engine is running
Drive in reverse for more than 100 m
explanation: It is illegal and unsafe to leave a vehicle unattended with the engine running, as it poses both safety and theft risks.

text: If you want to change lanes you must...
options: Switch on your indicator and change lanes
Give the necessary signal and after looking for other traffic, change lanes
Apply the brakes lightly and then change lanes
explanation: Before changing lanes, you must signal your intention, check mirrors and blind spots for other traffic, and then change lanes only when it is safe.

text: The fastest speed at which you may tow a vehicle with a rope is... km/h
explanation: When towing a vehicle with a rope, the maximum allowed speed is 30 km/h to ensure safety and control between both vehicles.

text: The fastest speed at which you may tow a vehicle with a rope is... km/h
explanation: When towing a vehicle with a rope, the maximum allowed speed is 30 km/h to ensure safety and control between both vehicles.

text: You may cross or enter a public road...
options: If the road is clear of traffic for a short distance
If the road is clear of traffic for a long distance and it can be done without obstructing traffic
In any manner as long as you use your flickers in time
explanation: You may only cross or enter a public road when there is enough clear distance for you to do so safely without obstructing other traffic.

text:
Your vehicle's headlights must be switched on:
(i) At any time of the day when you cannot see persons and vehicles 150 m in front of you
(ii) From sunset to sunrise
(iii) When it rains and you cannot see vehicles 100 m in front of you
options: (ii) only is correct
(i) and (ii) only are correct
All of the above are correct
explanation: Headlights must be used from sunset to sunrise and whenever visibility is reduced, such as in rain or when you cannot see 150 m ahead.

text: You may not drive into an intersection when...
options: The robot (traffic signal) is yellow and you are already in the intersection
The vehicle in front of you wants to turn right and the road is wide enough to pass on the left side
There is not enough space in the intersection to turn right without blocking other traffic
explanation: You may not enter an intersection if there is not enough space to clear it safely, as this can block other vehicles and cause traffic congestion.

text:
When you were involved in an accident you...
(i) Must immediately stop your vehicle
(ii) Must determine the damage to the vehicles
(iii) May refuse to give your name and address to anyone except the police
options: (i) and (ii) only are correct
(ii) only is correct
All of the above are correct
explanation: If you are involved in an accident, you must stop immediately and assess the damage. You are also required to provide your details to the other party and police — you may not refuse.

text:
When you were involved in an accident you...
(i) Must immediately stop your vehicle
(ii) Must see if someone is injured
(iii) May use a bit of alcohol for the shock
options: (i) and (ii) only are correct
(ii) only is correct
All of the above are correct
explanation: If you are involved in an accident, you must stop immediately and check if anyone is injured. It is illegal to consume alcohol after an accident, even for shock.

text:
When do you have the right of way?
(i) When you are within a traffic circle
(ii) When you have stopped first at a four-way stop
(iii) When you want to turn right at an intersection in a two-way road
options: (i) and (ii) only are correct
All of the above are correct
(i) only is correct
explanation: You have the right of way when you are already inside a traffic circle or when you were the first to stop at a four-way stop. Vehicles turning right must yield to oncoming traffic.

text: If you come across an emergency vehicle on the road sounding a siren you must...
options: Flash your headlight to warn other traffic
Give right of way to the emergency vehicle
Switch on your vehicle's emergency light and blow your hooter
explanation: When an emergency vehicle approaches with its siren on, you must yield the right of way by moving aside and allowing it to pass safely.

text: If you want to turn left with your vehicle, you must...
options: Slow down completely, stop and then turn
First move to the right to enable you to turn left easily
Give the necessary signal in good time
explanation: When turning left, you must signal your intention well in advance to warn other drivers and pedestrians of your move.

text: When you drive...
options: You must have both hands on the steering wheel
Your vision of the road and the traffic must be unobstructed
You must wear shoes with rubber soles
explanation: When driving, your view of the road and surrounding traffic must always be clear and unobstructed to ensure safe control of the vehicle.

text: Where may you legally stop with your vehicle?
options: 4 m from a tunnel
5 m from a pedestrian crossing
6 m from a railway crossing
explanation: You may stop your vehicle at least 6 metres from a railway crossing to ensure safety and prevent obstruction of trains or signals.

text:
You may not...
(i) Run the engine unattended
(ii) Use your vehicle without a cap on the fuel tank
(iii) Spin the wheels of your vehicle when pulling off
options: (ii) only is correct
All of the above are correct
explanation: All these actions are prohibited as they pose safety hazards — leaving the engine running unattended, driving without a fuel cap, or spinning the wheels are all unsafe and illegal.

text: What is important with regard to the hooter of your vehicle?
options: The tone and pitch of the sound may not change
Someone must hear it from a distance of at least 50 m
You may use it to get the attention of someone that you would like to offer a lift
explanation: The hooter of a vehicle must have a steady tone and pitch that does not change, ensuring it serves as a clear and consistent warning signal.

text: When the robot is red and the green arrow flashes to the right, it shows you that...
options: Only pedestrians may walk
If you want to turn right, you may go
All traffic must turn right there
explanation: A flashing green arrow to the right means you may turn right, even though the main red light is on, provided it is safe to do so and you yield to other traffic.

text:
You must stop your vehicle...
(i) On a public road at the signal of a person driving sheep
(ii) On a freeway when directed to do so by a traffic officer
(iii) On any road to avoid an accident
options: Only (ii) and (iii) are correct
Only (iii) is correct
All of the above are correct
explanation: You must stop your vehicle when signaled by a person driving animals, when instructed by a traffic officer, or to avoid an accident. All these situations require stopping for safety and legal compliance.

text: An accident in which no one has been injured must be reported within... hours.
explanation: If an accident occurs and no one is injured, it must still be reported to the nearest police station within 24 hours as required by law.

text: In which case is it permitted to travel with only the parking lights of your vehicle switched on?
options: When driving in heavy rain
When dusk is falling
In none of the above cases
explanation: You may not drive with only your parking lights on under any circumstances. Proper headlights must be used when visibility is reduced or during nighttime driving.

text: The only instance where you may stop on a freeway is...
options: To obey the road traffic sign
For a rest during a tiring journey
To pick up hitchhikers
explanation: You may only stop on a freeway when required to obey a road traffic sign, signal, or direction. Stopping for rest or to pick up passengers is prohibited.

text: When may a driver disobey a rule of the road?
options: Only when directed to do so by a traffic officer
Under no circumstances
If you are driving in an emergency situation
explanation: A driver may only disobey a rule of the road when explicitly instructed to do so by a traffic officer. This ensures that traffic remains safely directed under official control.

text: What is the duty of a driver when driving on a public road that has been divided into two or more roadways?
options: You may drive on any part of the roadway
You are allowed to drive on any part of the roadway after sunset, or when there is no other traffic on the road
Drive on the left-hand roadway unless directed or shown to do so by a traffic officer or traffic sign
explanation: Drivers must always keep to the left-hand side of a divided roadway unless a traffic sign or officer instructs otherwise.

text: When a motor vehicle is standing still, what must the driver do to make sure the motor vehicle does not move?
options: The gear lever must be put in the neutral position
The parking brake must be applied
The driver must hold the service brake
explanation: When a vehicle is stationary, the parking brake (handbrake) must be applied to prevent the vehicle from rolling or moving unintentionally.

text: What colour and size must flags be to indicate projections on a vehicle on a public road?
options: They can be any size as long as they are red
They must be red and at least 300 x 300 mm
They may be any colour as long as they are visible
explanation: Any projection extending from a vehicle must be marked with a red flag that is at least 300 mm by 300 mm to warn other road users.

text: A temporary sign...?
options: Need not be taken seriously at all times
Is of less importance to road users than a permanent sign
Has the same legal significance as a permanent sign
explanation: Temporary road signs carry the same legal authority as permanent ones and must be obeyed by all road users.

text: What is the duty of a driver about pedestrians at a pedestrian crossing?
options: A driver must only stop for a pedestrian waiting to enter the road at a pedestrian signal
A driver must yield right of way to a pedestrian crossing a pedestrian crossing
A driver must yield to all pedestrians wishing to cross over the roadway
explanation: Drivers must always yield right of way to pedestrians who are already crossing at a marked pedestrian crossing.

text: When is it permissible to allow a portion of the body to project beyond the vehicle?
options: Only for the driver to give hand signals
Only passengers may allow a portion of their bodies to project; they don’t need two hands on the steering wheel
When it is hot and the driver’s window is open
explanation: It is only permitted for the driver to extend an arm outside the vehicle when giving legal hand signals. No other part of the body may project beyond the vehicle.

text: What are the requirements for a vehicle being used with excessive noise?
options: There are no requirements with regards to excessive noise on a vehicle
No person shall operate a vehicle on a public road that causes any excessive noise
Excessive noise is acceptable during festive periods such as Christmas and New Year
explanation: According to South African traffic regulations, no person may drive a vehicle on a public road if it creates excessive or unnecessary noise that can disturb or endanger others.

text: How far behind a vehicle must the warning triangle be placed if your car breaks down?
options: At least 45 m
At least 10 m
At least 100 m
explanation: In South Africa, a warning triangle must be placed at least 45 metres behind a stationary or broken-down vehicle to alert approaching traffic of potential danger.

text: When driving a motor vehicle, the minimum safe following distance is...?
options: 12 meters at 120 kph (1 meter for every 10 kph)
A distance determined by the 2-second rule
A driver may follow as close as they want so that overtaking is easier when the gap is there
explanation: The safe following distance is determined by the 2-second rule — you should stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle in front of you to allow enough time to react and stop safely.

text: How far may you park from the left edge of a roadway outside an urban area?
options: A vehicle may not park on a public road unless in a parking bay
Not more than 450 mm from the edge of the roadway
Not more than 1 m from the edge of the roadway
explanation: Outside urban areas, vehicles may not park on a public road except in a designated parking bay, as parking on the shoulder or roadway could create a hazard for other traffic.

text: Show the correct statement: A driver may stop their vehicle on the roadway of a public road...?
options: When indicated by a traffic officer
In an intersection
In contravention with any road traffic sign
explanation: A driver may stop their vehicle on a public road only when instructed to do so by a traffic officer or under conditions that make it safe and lawful to do so.

text: What is the duty of a driver when refilling the fuel tank of a motor vehicle?
options: The driver may not allow the engine to run whilst flammable fuel is being transferred to the fuel tank
To check if they are filling the tank with diesel not petrol
Is allowed to start the vehicle while fuel is being pumped to check if the tank is full
explanation: It is prohibited to keep the engine running while refuelling because fuel vapours are highly flammable and can ignite, causing fire or explosion hazards.

text: Which one of the following statements is wrong?
options: The driver of a motor vehicle shall ensure that a child seated in a car wears a seatbelt, and where available use an appropriate child restraint
It is not the driver's responsibility to ensure a child is in a child restraint
If a seat not equipped with a seatbelt is available the driver shall ensure that a child 14 years and younger is seated on the rear seat
explanation: It is indeed the driver’s legal responsibility to ensure that any child in the vehicle is properly restrained using a seatbelt or approved child restraint where applicable.

text: The driver of a vehicle shall not cross a public road unless...?
options: They put on the indicator and then enter the road
They look in the rear view mirror, engage a gear and go
The road is clear of traffic for a safe distance, without obstructing or endangering other traffic
explanation: A driver may only cross or enter a public road when it can be done safely and without causing danger or obstruction to other traffic.

text: The following vehicle may not be used on a freeway...?
options: An animal drawn vehicle
An articulated motor vehicle
An abnormal loaded motor vehicle
explanation: Animal-drawn vehicles are not permitted on freeways in South Africa for safety reasons, as they move too slowly and can obstruct high-speed traffic.

text: A person under the influence of intoxicating liquor or a drug...?
options: May sit in the driver's seat of a vehicle of which the engine is running
May not sit in the driver's seat while the engine is running
May sleep in the driver's seat while the engine is running
explanation: A person under the influence of alcohol or drugs may not be in control of or seated in the driver’s seat of a vehicle with the engine running, as this is considered being in charge of a motor vehicle.

text: Which of the following statements are correct about a silencer?
options: With a small hole in it is acceptable
Need not be fitted only on heavy vehicles
Must be fitted to a vehicle to restrict the engine noise to a suitable noise level
explanation: All vehicles must be equipped with a functional silencer to reduce engine noise to acceptable levels. A damaged or missing silencer makes a vehicle unroadworthy.

text: What is the minimum distance stop lamps must be visible to a person with normal eyesight in sunlight?
explanation: In South Africa, stop lamps must be visible from at least 30 metres in bright sunlight to ensure that following drivers can clearly see when a vehicle is braking.

text: When driving a vehicle alone, what documents must you carry with you?
options: Any person's valid driver's licence if you only have a learner's licence
Your original valid driver's licence
A certified copy of your driver's licence and ID document
explanation: When driving alone, you must carry your original valid driver’s licence with you at all times as proof of legal authorization to operate a motor vehicle.

text: When are you allowed to drive on the right-hand side of a freeway?
options: When you are driving 120 kph
At any time as long as you don’t stop in the right-hand lane
Only when overtaking another vehicle
explanation: On a freeway, drivers must keep to the left-hand lane except when overtaking. The right-hand lane is reserved solely for overtaking other vehicles.

text: How long must a flicker be displayed?
options: For long enough to show vehicles or persons approaching you of your intentions
For about 3 minutes
For about 2 minutes
explanation: Indicators (flickers) must be displayed long enough to clearly show other road users your intention to turn or change lanes, giving them time to react safely.

text: When may you pass another vehicle that has stopped at a pedestrian crossing?
options: You can pass if it’s safe to do so
It is prohibited to pass any vehicle that has stopped at a pedestrian crossing
You may pass only once the pedestrian has crossed
explanation: It is illegal to pass a vehicle that has stopped at a pedestrian crossing because there may be pedestrians crossing in front of it. Passing in this situation endangers pedestrians and violates road safety laws.

text: How far may you park from the left edge of a roadway outside an urban area?
options: A vehicle may not park on a public road unless in a parking bay
Not more than 450 mm from the edge of the roadway
Not more than 1 m from the edge of the roadway
explanation: Outside urban areas, vehicles may not park on a public road except in a designated parking bay, as parking on the shoulder or roadway could create a hazard for other traffic.

text: Which statement is False? A vehicle may be used on a public road if...
options: The battery and electrical wiring are properly installed
The fuel cap is effective and closed
The fuel tank is defective
explanation: A vehicle may not be used on a public road if the fuel tank is defective. All fuel system components must be in proper working condition to prevent leaks and fire hazards.

text: You are in heavy traffic in the right-hand lane. The car in front wants to turn into his driveway and has stopped, waiting for heavy oncoming traffic. What do you do?
options: Wait behind the car until you get the opportunity to pass, and when it’s safe, proceed
Switch on your left flicker and move to the left lane
Hoot, wave and pass
explanation: In this situation, you must remain patient and wait behind the vehicle ahead until it is safe to pass. Attempting to move left or hoot to pressure the driver could be dangerous or illegal in heavy traffic.

text: The use of a temporary sign implies that for some reason...?
options: The rules of the road do not apply.
The situation on the road is not normal.
Traffic must move slowly.
explanation: Temporary road signs are used when normal road conditions are disrupted, such as during construction, accidents, or maintenance. They warn drivers that special caution or altered behavior is required.

text: How far must you be parked from either side of a fire hydrant?
options: 1.5 meter
750mm
1 meter
explanation: Drivers must park at least 1.5 meters away from a fire hydrant on either side to ensure that emergency services have clear access in case of a fire.

text: What is the difference between these road markings?
options: There is no difference between the two and both show you that you may not pass other vehicles
Both show you that you may not pass other vehicles but you will find a single line on all roads and double lines on freeways only
A single line shows you that you may not pass other vehicles while a double line also shows you that you may not drive over it to turn into a yard or anything else
explanation: A single solid line prohibits overtaking, while a double solid line also prohibits crossing for any reason, including turning into a driveway or yard.

text: This road marking is a…
options: Pedestrian crossing where you must stop for pedestrians
Painted island where you are not allowed to drive on or stop
Chevron that indicates a curve to the left
explanation: This marking indicates a painted island used to separate traffic or guide vehicles. You may not drive, stop, or park on it.

text: If you are driving towards a mini-circle and there are also vehicles from the other three sides, you…
options: Must always wait for the vehicle from your right before you drive on
May drive on if you were the first vehicle over the line
Must stop with all the vehicles and only drive on when it is safe
explanation: At a mini-circle, the first vehicle to reach the line has the right of way to proceed first. Normal 'give way to the right' rules apply only when vehicles reach the line at the same time.

text: This road marking shows you that…
options: You are not allowed to pass another vehicle there
A line is going to begin which prohibits you from passing
The lane splits into more lanes in the direction of the arrow
explanation: This marking with broken lines that close together warns drivers that a no-overtaking line is about to start ahead. Prepare to stay in your lane and avoid passing.

text: This road marking shows you that only… may park there
options: Minibuses
Municipal buses
Motorcycles
explanation: The letters 'MB' on a yellow road marking indicate a parking area reserved exclusively for minibuses.

text: Road marking GM1 in this sketch…
options: Shows the lanes for road users
Divides the road into two sections
Is only found in a parking area
explanation: The GM1 road marking is a broken white line that indicates lane divisions for vehicles traveling in the same direction.

text: This arrow shows you that you…
options: Must turn right from the lane
Can turn right or move straight on if it is safe
Can still change lanes if you want to go on straight
explanation: A single directional arrow painted in the lane indicates that you must follow that direction. In this case, vehicles in that lane must turn right.

text: When you see this road marking, you…
options: May not park there because it is parking for ambulances only
May not park there at all because it’s a no stopping road marking
Know it is a lane reserved for emergency vehicles
explanation: A continuous yellow line along the edge of the road indicates a no stopping zone. You may not stop, park, or wait at any time on this section of the road.

text: Road marking RTM 1 shows you that…
options: If you are driving in car A, you must stop before this line
If you are driving in car A, you must reduce speed and ride on if it is safe
If you are driving in car B, you can pass car A if there are no other vehicles in the intersection
explanation: RTM 1 is a solid stop line marking. Drivers must bring their vehicles to a complete stop before this line when approaching a stop sign or red traffic light.

text: Road markings RTM3 in the sketch…
options: Show you that you may not stop further than the front one of the two
Are the lines where pedestrians walk
Are lines that indicate another traffic line
explanation: RTM3 markings are the white lines indicating a pedestrian crossing. Pedestrians have the right of way within these lines.

text: This road marking shows that you must…
options: Stop
Look out for school kids
Give right of way to all users of the road and possibly also trains
explanation: This is a yield (give way) marking. It indicates that you must slow down and give right of way to all road users on the main road, and in some cases to trains at crossings.

text: This road marking shows you that…
options: The road surface is uneven
Traffic may not overtake or cross it on either side
It is a lane reserved for buses only
explanation: A double solid white line indicates that overtaking or crossing the line is strictly prohibited for traffic in both directions.

text: This road marking shows you that only… may park there
options: Buses
Business vehicles
Minibuses
explanation: A yellow road marking with the letter 'B' indicates a parking bay reserved exclusively for buses.

text: This road marking shows you that only… may park there
options: Goods vehicles that load or unload
Motor cars that load or unload
Construction vehicles

explanation: Indicators communicate your intention; they do not grant right of way.

text: Which of the following statements are correct?
options: Vehicle lights must be switched on at sunrise.
Use emergency warning flashing lights only when the vehicle is stationary in a hazardous position or when travelling in an emergency situation.
Use the vehicle's bright beams
explanation: Hazard lights are for stationary hazards or authorised emergencies.

text:
With regards to seating in a light or heavy motor vehicle, which of the following statements are correct? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Each seated adult needs 380 mm seat width.
ii. Two children 3–6 years count as one adult passenger.
iii. Three children 6–13 years count as two adult passengers.
iv. Each person counts as a passenger regardless of age.
options: Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (i) and (iv) are correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
explanation: Seat width and child-to-adult passenger equivalences apply as stated.

text: What is the color of a vehicle's reverse light(s), located externally at the back of the vehicle?
options: Red
Amber (orange/yellow)
White
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Reverse lamps are white.

text: A motor vehicle may not be used on a public road ...
options: if the fuel tank, carburettor, fuel receptacle or fuel pipes are defective or so exposed that they constitute a danger.
unless the electrical wiring and battery are properly installed, insulated and maintained.
Both of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Both fuel system safety and electrical safety are compulsory.

text: You may make a U-turn on a highway ...
options: if you missed the exit.
if you see that traffic is backed up due to an accident.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: U-turns are not permitted on highways.

text:
You may not overtake another vehicle … (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. if you must drive over a solid white line.
ii. by driving on the shoulder of the road.
iii. if it is waiting for pedestrians to cross the road.
iv. at a stop sign.
options: Only (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct.
Only (iii) and (iv) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: All listed situations prohibit overtaking.

text: Regarding overall vehicle length, a bus-train shall not exceed ...
explanation: The maximum permitted overall length for a bus-train is 22 m.

text: Regarding overall vehicle width, a goods vehicle with a GVM of 12000kg or more, shall not exceed ...
explanation: The width limit for large goods vehicles is 2.6 m.

text: If the overall length of a motor vehicle, or combination of motor vehicles, exceeds 7m it must be fitted with yellow reflective strips on each side or with yellow retro-reflectors no more than ... apart.
options: 1m
explanation: Side reflectors/strips must be spaced at intervals not exceeding 3.6 m.

text: Heavy motor vehicles must at all times maintain a ... following distance behind other vehicles.
options: one vehicle length
2-second
3-second
explanation: A 3-second following distance is the standard safe gap for heavy vehicles.

text: You are allowed to exceed an indicated speed limit, or the general speed limit, by ...
options: 5km/h.
10km/h.
20km/h.
You are not allowed to exceed the speed limit at all.
explanation: Speed limits are legal maxima; exceeding them is unlawful.

text:
At an intersection where the traffic light displays a steady green disc, you have right of way if you are ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. driving straight ahead.
ii. turning left, unless you are channelled through a slipway.
iii. turning right, unless the traffic light also displays a green arrow to the right.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: A steady green gives right of way straight ahead and for left turns (except via slipways). Right turns must still yield unless separately arrowed.

text: Where a goods vehicle is temporarily stationary on the roadway of a public road it is required that the driver must …
options: display one emergency waring sign in the front and one at the back of the vehicle.
put out a red fire extinguisher to warn traffic.
display at least one emergency warning sign at the back of the vehicle.
explanation: A stationary goods vehicle must display at least one warning triangle behind it.

text: What type of heavy motor vehicle or combination of motor vehicles are restricted to travel at a maximum speed of 80km/h?
options: An articulated motor vehicle of which the gross combination mass of truck-tractor exceeds 9000kg.
Only vehicles carrying goods which belong to the government and traffic police.
Any heavy motor vehicle carrying goods.
explanation: Articulated vehicles where the truck-tractor’s GCM exceeds 9000 kg are limited to 80 km/h.

text: Which of the following statements is correct? A silencer ...
options: need not be fitted.
with a small hole is acceptable.
must be fitted to a vehicle to restrict engine noise to acceptable levels.
explanation: A functioning exhaust silencer is compulsory to reduce noise.

text: When driving a motor vehicle, what is the minimum safe following distance to maintain when following another vehicle?
options: A distance determined by means of the two-second rule.
A driver may drive as close as possible so that overtaking will be easier.
Five metres at 100km/h.
explanation: Use at least the two-second rule; increase it in poor conditions.

text: On which side of the roadway may you drive if the roadway is wide enough without endangering other traffic?
options: A driver shall drive on the left side of the roadway.
A driver may encroach or drive on the right-hand of a roadway if the car in front is driving slowly.
A driver may drive on the right-hand side provided there is no traffic.
explanation: Keep left at all times except when overtaking or instructed otherwise.

text: How far may you park from the left edge of the roadway outside an urban area?
options: Not more than 450mm from the edge of the roadway.
A vehicle may not be parked in the roadway unless in a parking area.
Not more than 1m from the edge of the roadway.
explanation: Outside urban areas you may not park on the roadway except in a demarcated bay.

text: When is overtaking prohibited?
options: When approaching any place where passing could cause a hazard to traffic approaching from the opposite direction.
When passing a school.
When driving at night.
explanation: Do not overtake where visibility or space makes it hazardous for oncoming traffic.

text: When moving off from a stationary position at the side of the road, what is the responsibility of the driver?
options: The driver must ensure that it is safe and that he/she will not interfere with traffic approaching from any direction.
The driver must join other traffic as quickly as possible.
The driver must indicate his/her intention and then move off.
explanation: You must first ensure it’s safe and won’t impede any traffic before moving off.

text: What should a driver consider when following another vehicle?
options: The driver should be able to see the rear tyres of the vehicle in front.
The driver should follow another vehicle keeping three car lengths behind.
The driver should follow at a safe distance and be able to stop safely if the vehicle in front slows or stops.
explanation: Maintain a gap that allows safe stopping in emergencies.

text: Trailers of which the gross vehicle mass does not exceed 10000kg …
options: shall be fitted with yellow reflective material to the sides and the rear of the vehicle.
shall be fitted with yellow reflective material to the sides of the vehicle only.
are not required to fit yellow reflective material to the vehicle.
explanation: Trailers up to 10 000 kg GVM require yellow reflective material on sides and rear.

text: What is the duty of a driver when re-filling the fuel tank with petrol or inflammable fuel?
options: He/she may only allow the engine to run if diesel is being transferred to the fuel tank.
He/she may start the engine whilst petrol or other inflammable fuel is being transferred to check if the fuel tank is full.
The driver may not cause or allow the engine to run whilst petrol or other inflammable fuel is being transferred to the fuel tank.
explanation: The engine must be switched off during refuelling for safety.

text: What is the requirement regarding noise caused by a motor vehicle?
options: A person may operate a vehicle causing excessive noise, but only at night.
No person shall operate a vehicle on a public road in such a manner that it causes excessive noise.
A person may operate a vehicle causing excessive noise outside of town.
explanation: Excessive noise from a vehicle is prohibited anywhere on public roads.

text: Headlamps, rear lamps and number plate lamps of light and heavy motor vehicles must be switched on ...
options: between sunset and sunrise.
during peak hours.
at all times.
explanation: Lights must be on from sunset to sunrise and when visibility is poor.

text: Which statement is correct?
options: A heavy motor vehicle may not be used on a public road if it is fitted with a spot lamp which can emit a beam of light that can be deflected in any direction.
A heavy motor vehicle may be fitted with a spot lamp to warn others of roadworks.
A heavy motor vehicle may be fitted with a spot lamp to add an extra beam when it is raining.
explanation: Adjustable spot lamps are generally prohibited on heavy motor vehicles on public roads.

text: If you have a driving licence and you are driving a vehicle, where should the licence document be?
options: In a safe place at home.
With you in the vehicle.
In a safe place at home and you should have a copy with you.
explanation: You must carry your licence when driving and produce it on demand.

text: No person driving a vehicle on a public road may …
options: leave a vehicle unattended without applying its parking brake to prevent it from moving from the position in which it was left.
leave a vehicle unattended without applying its parking brake to prevent it from moving further than 30cm from the position in which it was left.
leave a vehicle unattended without applying its service brake to prevent it from moving.
explanation: Always secure a parked vehicle with the parking brake.

text: Which one of the following statements is correct?
options: Pedal cycles are not permitted on a freeway.
Racing cycles may be ridden on a freeway during the day only.
Pedal cycles may only be ridden on the shoulder of the freeway.
explanation: Pedal cycles are prohibited on freeways.

text:
A driver may not stop their vehicle on the roadway of a public road … (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. when instructed to do so by a traffic officer.
ii. in an intersection.
iii. in contravention with any road traffic sign.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (iii) is correct.
explanation: Stopping in an intersection or contrary to a traffic sign is prohibited.

text: You are permitted to …
options: use your mobile phone using headgear to communicate.
drive your vehicle on the pavement if there are no pedestrians around.
use the hooter of your vehicle to attract pedestrians you want to pick up.
explanation: Hands-free use is allowed; handheld use and pavement driving are not.

text: A light or heavy motor vehicle must be equipped with an efficient exhaust silencer, which …
options: does not have to be maintained, as long as it does not make a noise.
must be so maintained that it does not cause a vibration in the cab.
must be so maintained that the exhaust gas or smoke does not leak into the driving cab or passenger compartment of the vehicle.
explanation: The silencer must prevent exhaust gases entering the cab or passenger area.

text: You are caught in slow-moving heavy traffic in the right lane of a busy urban road. The car in front wants to turn right into a driveway and is waiting. What should you do?
options: Switch on your left indicator and move into the left lane.
Wait behind the car until you get an opportunity to pass on the left, or to proceed.
Hoot and pass to the left.
explanation: Be patient and wait until it’s safe to pass or proceed.

text: When is it permissible to park in a "no stopping" area?
options: Parking is permissible, however, only stopping is not permissible.
Only if no other parking area is available.
It is not permissible to park where stopping is not permitted.
explanation: "No stopping" also prohibits parking.

text: When flags have to be used to indicate projections ...
options: they must be any size red flag.
they may be any colour as long as they are visible.
they must be red and at least 300mm x 300mm.
explanation: Daytime projection markings require red flags of at least 300×300 mm.

text: If travelling in a goods vehicle towing a trailer, how many emergency warning signs (triangles) must you carry?
options: Only one.
A minimum of two warning signs (triangles).
Warning triangles are not compulsory.
explanation: A towing goods vehicle must carry at least two warning triangles.

text: Which of the following vehicles are not allowed on a freeway?
options: A vehicle driven by a learner driver.
A tractor, except when it is used in connection with construction or maintenance of the freeway.
A vehicle used for the conveyance of school children.
explanation: Tractors are prohibited except when involved in freeway construction/maintenance.

text: When is it permissible to allow a portion of the body to protrude beyond a vehicle?
options: Only for the driver to give a hand signal.
Only passengers may have a portion of their body protruding.
When it is hot and the driver's window is open.
explanation: Only lawful hand signals by the driver are allowed; otherwise keep limbs inside.

text: Which statement is true?
options: A person may only drive a motor vehicle in such a way that it causes excessive noise in an urban area.
A person may only drive a motor vehicle in such a way that it causes excessive noise outside a built up area.
No person shall operate a vehicle on a public road in such a manner as to cause excessive noise.
explanation: Excessive vehicle noise is unlawful anywhere on public roads.

text: What type of brakes must be fitted on a light or heavy motor vehicle?
options: Service brake, parking brake and emergency brake.
Parking brake only.
Service brake only.
explanation: Vehicles require service, parking, and (where applicable) emergency braking systems.

text: What is the requirement for exhaust silencers?
options: The driver must ensure that no gas or smoke leaks into the cab or passenger compartment of the vehicle.
Exhaust silencers must be professionally checked once a year.
The exhaust silencer must not allow the exhaust gas to be emitted to the right rear of the vehicle.
explanation: Exhaust gases must not leak into the cab or passenger compartment.

text: Whilst the vehicle is in motion a driver may ...
options: not hold a cell phone in their hand or with any other part of the body.
type an SMS.
hold a cell phone provided the driver keeps at least one hand on the steering wheel.
explanation: Hand-held phone use (including holding by any body part) is prohibited while driving.

text: What is legal with regard to towing another vehicle with a motorcycle?
options: You may tow it with a 750cc motorcycle.
You may tow it with a motor tricycle.
You may not tow it with any motorcycle.
explanation: Motorcycles are not permitted to tow another vehicle on public roads.

text: You violate the traffic law if you ride your motorcycle or motor tricycle …
options: conveying 2 adult persons in the sidecar.
with a code 1 learner's licence without supervision, on a motorcycle with a sidecar, when seating is available in the sidecar.
next to another motorcycle on a one-way street, while both of you are travelling in a separate lane.
explanation: Riding abreast alongside another vehicle in the same lane is prohibited.

text: Your motorcycle must have …
options: 1 number plate in the front only.
1 number plate at the rear only.
1 number plate in the front and 1 at the rear.
explanation: Motorcycles are required to display a rear number plate only.

text:
When is it an offence when you are the holder of a learner's licence for a motorcycle? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. You ride on your own motorcycle next to your instructor.

ii. You keep only one hand on the handlebars for the entire trip.

iii. You ride at 80km/h outside built-up areas.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Learners may not ride alongside an instructor and must keep proper control; speed alone outside built-up areas is not the offence stated.

text: If your motorcycle has an engine size of ... and smaller, you may not use it on a freeway.
options: 50cc
125cc
250cc
explanation: Motorcycles ≤50cc are prohibited from using freeways.

text: When may you as the holder of a learner's licence carry a passenger on your motorcycle?
options: For short journeys if you do not exceed the speed limit.
When a motorcycle has a cylinder capacity of at least 100cc.
Never.
explanation: Learner motorcycle riders may not carry passengers.

text: When you ride your motorcycle, you are not allowed to …
options: have only one hand on the handlebars at times.
have one wheel of the motorcycle off the ground.
carry a passenger on a 125cc motorcycle.
explanation: Riding on one wheel (‘wheelies’) is unsafe and unlawful on public roads.

text: When you ride a motorcycle …
options: you must have two hands on the handlebars at all times.
your view of the road and the traffic must be unobstructed.
you must wear shoes with rubber soles.
explanation: Your view must be unobstructed; having two hands is expected for control but the legal requirement centers on unobstructed view.

text: A load carried on a motorcycle may not project more than ... on either side of the wheels.
options: 150mm
300mm
450mm
explanation: Side projection is limited to 450 mm from either wheel.

text:
Which of the following statements are true? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Motorcyclists must ride in single file in a lane.

ii. Motorcyclists may not ride alongside another vehicle in a lane, except for overtaking.

iii. Two motorcycles may not overtake another vehicle at the same time.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (iii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: All three restrictions apply for safety and order in traffic.

text: If you are under the age of 18, you may only ride a motorcycle with a cylinder capacity not exceeding ...
options: 50cc.
explanation: Under 18s are restricted to motorcycles not exceeding 125 cc.

text: When riding a motorcycle on a public road, the headlights must be switched on ...
options: from sunset to sunrise.
at all times.
at any time when, due to unfavourable conditions, persons and vehicles are not clearly discernible at a distance of 150m.
explanation: Motorcycle headlights must be on at all times for conspicuity.

text:
Someone with a learner's licence for a motorcycle, may not … (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. ride at night time.

ii. carry a passenger.

iii. ride on a public road, unless supervised by someone with a valid driver's licence of the same code.
options: Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: The key absolute prohibition is carrying a passenger; supervision and night-riding depend on local code specifics.

text: You may not use a motorcycle with an engine size of 200cc or more on a public road, unless the distance between the outside edges of the handlebars is …
options: between 200mm and 600mm.
between 500mm and 800mm.
between 600mm and 800mm.
explanation: For ≥200 cc motorcycles, handlebar width must be 600–800 mm.

text: You may not use a motorcycle with an engine size of less than 200cc on a public road, unless the distance between the outside edges of the handlebars is …
options: between 200mm and 600mm.
between 500mm and 800mm.
between 600mm and 800mm.
explanation: For <200 cc motorcycles, handlebar width must be 500–800 mm.

text:
You may not use a motorcycle on a public road of which the outer ends of the handgrips on the handlebars are …. (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. higher than 300mm above the seat height.

ii. higher than 500mm above the seat height.

iii. lower than the seat height.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (iii) is correct.
explanation: Bars more than 500 mm above seat height or lower than seat height are prohibited.

text: How many independent brake systems must a motorcycle have?
explanation: Front and rear braking systems are required.

text: When riding a motorcycle on a public road, with a sidecar attached, who must wear a safety helmet?
options: Only the passenger(s) in the sidecar.
Only the rider.
The rider and all passengers.
explanation: Helmets are compulsory for the rider and all passengers.

text: The rider of a motorcycle need not wear a safety helmet when ...
options: the motorcycle is equipped with a seat belt.
the engine of the motorcycle is switched off.
Both of the above are correct.
explanation: When stationary with engine off, or if seat-belt equipped (rare), helmet use is not mandated.

text: Goods carried on a motorcycle may not project more than ... to the outside of the wheel of the sidecar.
options: 150mm
300mm
450mm
explanation: Sidecar-side projection is limited to 300 mm.

text: You may not ride a motorcycle, motorcycle with a sidecar, or motor tricycle on a public road, unless it is fitted on the rear with ...
options: a red retro-reflector.
2 red retro-reflectors
1 white retro-reflector and 1 red retro-reflector.
explanation: At least one red rear retro-reflector is mandatory.

text: How many persons are allowed to ride on a motorcycle, excluding persons riding in a sidecar attached to such motorcycle?
options: As many persons as can be carried on the seat(s).
1 Adult and a maximum of 2 children.
explanation: A rider plus one passenger (if the motorcycle is designed for it) is the limit.

text: How many adult persons are allowed to be carried in a sidecar, attached to a motorcycle, if you are not riding faster than 30km/h?
explanation: Up to two adults may be carried in the sidecar at low speed limits.

text: Which of the following statements are applicable to sidecars attached to motorcycles?
options: A sidecar must only be attached to the left side of a motorcycle.
No sidecar may be attached to a motorcycle with an engine size of 125cc or less.
Both of the above are correct.
explanation: In left-hand traffic, sidecars must be attached on the left; engine-size prohibition stated is not generally applicable.

text: Goods may not be carried on a motorcycle that they protrude more than ... to the rear of the axle of the rear wheel.
options: 450mm
600mm
900mm
explanation: Rearward projection on motorcycles is limited to 900 mm.

text: A motorcycle with an engine capacity not exceeding 50cc must be fitted with ... tyres.
options: Pneumatic
Retreaded
radial steel
explanation: 50 cc class motorcycles must use pneumatic tyres.

text: What is the maximum distance allowed for goods, transported on a motorcycle, to project beyond the front of the axle of the front wheel?
options: 300mm
450mm
600mm
You may not carry goods that project to the front of a motorcycle.
explanation: Front projection is limited to 600 mm beyond the front wheel axle.

text: On motorcycles with an engine size of 50cc or less, the tread pattern of the tyres must be visible ...
options: on at least 50% of the tyre's width.
on at least 80% of the tyre's width.
across the tyre's entire width over the full circumference of the tyre.
explanation: For ≤50 cc motorcycles, tread must be visible over at least 80% of width.

text:
Which of the following statements are true? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. The rider of a motorcycle may not carry persons or animals in front of the rider.

ii. The rider of a motorcycle may carry a small, non-bulky item in front, only if it is securely attached to the motorcycle.

iii. The rider of a motorcycle may not carry any parcels in front of the rider that obstructs the rider's view.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: All three statements reflect safe and lawful carriage rules for riders.

text: A motorcycle with an engine size of ... or less may not carry passengers.
options: 50cc
125cc
250cc
explanation: Motorcycles ≤50 cc may not carry passengers.

text: You may transport goods on a light or heavy motor vehicle that they …
options: Protrude 2,0m at the rear.
Protrude 450mm in the front.
Are with the vehicle 2,5m wide.
explanation: The maximum legal width of a vehicle including its load is 2.5 m.

text: You may carry passengers in a vehicle that is being towed … SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
All of the above is correct.
explanation: Passengers may be carried only if the towed vehicle is a semi-trailer.

text: You may not reverse your vehicle for further than …
options: If it is safe to do so.
explanation: Reversing is only permitted as far as it can be done safely.

text: At an intersection …
options: You must yield to oncoming traffic if you want to turn right.
Vehicles have right of way over pedestrians.
You can use a stop sign as a yield sign if there is no other traffic.
explanation: When turning right, yield to oncoming traffic before proceeding.

text: If you see that someone wants to overtake you, you must … SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Keep left as far as safe and do not accelerate while being overtaken.

text: When you drive …
options: You must have two hands on the steering wheel.
Your view of the road and the traffic must be unobstructed.
You must wear shoes with rubber soles.
explanation: A clear, unobstructed view of the road is a legal requirement.

text: Where may you legally stop your vehicle?
options: 4 m from a tunnel.
5 m from a pedestrian crossing.
6 m from a railway crossing.
explanation: Stopping within 6 m of a railway crossing is not allowed; beyond that is permitted.

text: You may not … SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
options: Only (i) and (ii) are not allowed.
Only (ii) is not allowed.
None of the above are allowed.
explanation: Running the engine unattended, lacking a fuel-cap, or spinning wheels are all prohibited.

text: What is the maximum period of time that a vehicle may be parked in one place on a road outside urban areas?
options: 24 hours
48 hours
7 days
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Outside urban areas, vehicles may not remain parked longer than 24 hours.

text: What is important with regard to the hooter of your vehicle?
options: The tone of the sound (pitch) may not change.
Someone must hear it from a distance of at least 45 m.
You may use it to get the attention of someone that you would like to offer a lift.
explanation: A vehicle hooter must maintain a constant tone; variable-pitch or musical horns are illegal.

text: You may ...
options: Drive your vehicle on the sidewalk.
Allow your vehicle to move backwards only if it is safe to do so.
Leave the engine of your vehicle running when you put petrol in it.
explanation: Reversing is allowed only when it can be done safely and without danger.

text: A motor vehicle licence and licence disc is valid for a period of ...
options: 21 days.
90 days.
12 months.
24 months.
explanation: Licence discs are valid for 12 months and must be renewed annually.

text: The maximum distance between two vehicles when one is towing the other is ...
explanation: The legal maximum towing-rope distance is 3.5 metres.

text: The lights of a vehicle, parked on a public road between sunset and sunrise, need not be kept lighted when the vehicle is parked … SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
options: Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Parking lights are not needed if parked near street lighting, beside the roadway, or in a marked area.

text: It is illegal when you drive your car and a passenger ...
options: Sits directly behind you when you only have a learner's licence.
Fiddles with the motor radio's volume knob.
Rides on the bumper of your vehicle.
explanation: Carrying passengers on the outside of a moving vehicle is strictly prohibited.

text: The only instance where you may stop on a freeway is ...
options: To obey a road traffic sign.
For a rest during a tiring journey.
To pick up hitchhikers.
explanation: Stopping on a freeway is allowed only to obey signs, signals, or a lawful instruction.

text: You are not allowed to stop ...
options: On the pavement.
With the front of your vehicle facing oncoming traffic.
Next to any obstruction in the road.
explanation: Parking or stopping against the direction of traffic flow is illegal.

text: When you were involved in an accident you … SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Drivers involved in an accident must stop immediately and determine the damage caused.

text: You may put your arm out the window, whilst driving, to … SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
options: Only (ii) is correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Hand signals are permitted only for legal signalling purposes.

text: What is the maximum period of time that a vehicle may be parked in one place on a road within an urban area?
options: 24 hours
48 hours
7 days
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Within urban areas, a vehicle may not stay parked longer than seven days.

text: When turning right at an intersection … SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
options: Only (ii) and (iv) are correct.
Only (iv) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: When turning right, always yield to oncoming traffic before proceeding.

text: Unless otherwise indicated by a road sign, what is the speed limit on freeways?
options: 80 km/h
100 km/h
120 km/h
explanation: The general freeway speed limit for light motor vehicles is 120 km/h.

text: You may not overtake another vehicle … SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Overtaking on a solid line, in tunnels, on painted islands, or with poor visibility is illegal.

text: Unless otherwise indicated by a road sign, the speed limit in a residential area is ...
options: 40 km/h.
60 km/h.
80 km/h.
explanation: Residential speed limits are generally 60 km/h unless posted otherwise.

text: What does the speed limit mean?
options: The fastest speed that you may drive on a specific road.
The slowest speed that you may drive on a specific road.
The average speed that you should maintain with your vehicle on a specific road.
explanation: The speed limit is the legal maximum, not a target or minimum.

text: When are you exempt of wearing a seat belt?
options: When you are busy parking your vehicle.
If you are younger than 14 years of age.
If you are pregnant.
explanation: Seat-belt use is not required only during low-speed parking manoeuvres.

text: You may use the hooter of your vehicle …
options: To attract a traffic officer's attention.
To avoid a collision.
To warn the driver in front of you when it is their turn to move off.
explanation: A hooter should be used only to prevent an accident, not as a courtesy or alert signal.

text: When towing another vehicle …
options: Only two people are allowed in the towed vehicle.
A tractor may carry 10 people on a semi-trailer, if travelling at 30 km/h.
On the freeway, you may tow a vehicle with a tow-rope no faster than 30 km/h, even if the minimum speed of that portion of the freeway is 50 km/h.
explanation: A tractor towing a semi-trailer may carry up to 10 people at low speed under specific conditions.

text: No reckless or negligent driving is allowed on public roads. What does this mean?
options: You may not exceed the speed limit.
You may not drive in a manner that wilfully disregards the safety of other road users, pedestrians or property.
You may not skip a stop street sign.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Reckless driving covers all acts showing disregard for traffic laws or safety.

text: A combination of motor vehicles is restricted to a drawing vehicle, and … SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: A legal vehicle combination may include a towing vehicle with up to two trailers, or one motor vehicle and trailer in emergencies.

text: How close to a demarcated pedestrian crossing may you park?
options: Not within 6m from the white lines.
Not within 9m of the approach side.
There is no parking distance, as long as you do not park on the actual pedestrian crossing.
explanation: Keep at least 9 m back on the approach side to ensure visibility and pedestrian safety.

text:
Someone with a learner's licence for a light or heavy motor vehicle, may not …  (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. drive at night time.
ii. drive on a freeway.
iii. have more than 1 passenger in the vehicle.
iv. drive a vehicle on a public road, unless supervised by someone with a valid driver's licence of the same code.
options: Only (ii) and (iv) are correct.
Only (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct.
Only (iv) is correct.
explanation: The universal restriction is supervision by a licensed driver of the same code.

text: How close to a bridge may a driver park their vehicle?
options: Not within 6m from the bridge.
Not within 9m from the bridge.
Not within 10m from the bridge.
explanation: Parking is prohibited within 6 m of a bridge to avoid obstruction.

text: How far away from a fire hydrant may you park your vehicle?
options: At least 450mm away on either side of the hydrant.
At least 1,5m away on either side of the hydrant.
At least 3m away on either side of the hydrant.
explanation: A 1.5 m clearance ensures emergency access to the hydrant.

text: When you drive in heavy fog during the day, you should switch on your vehicle's ...
options: parking lights.
headlights, set to the dipped beam.
headlights, set to the main beam.
explanation: Dipped beams improve your visibility without dazzling others.

text: Which of the following is a good example of defensive driving?
options: To put one car length between you and the car ahead of you.
To check your mirrors a couple of times during your trip.
To keep your eyes moving, looking for possible hazards.
explanation: Constant scanning helps you anticipate and avoid hazards.

text: In which of these conditions would you increase your following distance?
options: When driving on a slippery road.
When following a motorcycle.
When following a truck or a vehicle pulling a trailer.
All of the above.
explanation: Reduced traction or limited visibility requires more space to react.

text: If you are travelling at a speed of 80km/h on a freeway and the speed limit is 120km/h, in which lane must you drive?
options: Any lane that you prefer.
In the left-hand lane, unless you are overtaking another vehicle.
In the middle lane.
explanation: Keep left, pass right is the basic freeway rule.

text: When more than one vehicle arrives at a 4-way stop intersection, which vehicle has right of way?
options: The vehicle that moves off the fastest.
Each vehicle in the order that they have stopped.
The vehicle on your right.
explanation: Vehicles proceed in the order they stopped to keep it fair and predictable.

text: If you intend to pull into a driveway just past an intersection, when should you signal (indicate)?
options: As soon as you have crossed the intersection.
Before you cross the intersection.
As soon as you start turning.
In the middle of the intersection.
explanation: Indicate after the intersection to avoid misleading other drivers.

text: At an intersection with traffic signals (robots) that are out of order, you must ...
options: treat it like a four-way stop.
treat it like a yield sign.
ignore it if you are driving on the road that has priority.
explanation: A dead robot = four-way stop for safety and order.

text: If you have already entered an intersection and the traffic light changes, you should ...
options: stop in the intersection.
proceed and clear the intersection.
flash your lights through the intersection.
sound your hooter through the intersection.
explanation: Clear the intersection safely to avoid blocking cross-traffic.

text: When may you legally block an intersection?
options: During rush hour traffic.
If you've entered an intersection when the light was still green.
When the light is amber.
You may not block an intersection at any time.
explanation: Entering without space to clear is illegal and causes gridlock.

text: When a traffic officer directs you to drive through a red traffic light, what should you do?
options: Never ignore traffic signals. You must stop at a red light.
Drive through the red light.
Wait for the light to turn green.
explanation: A lawful instruction from a traffic officer overrides signals.

text: If you have a green light, but traffic is backed up into the intersection, you should ...
options: enter the intersection and hope traffic clears before the light changes.
wait until traffic clears before entering the intersection.
try to go around the traffic.
sound your horn to clear the intersection.
explanation: Only enter when you can clear completely to avoid blocking.

text: When should you obey a construction flagger's instructions?
options: At all times in construction zones.
lf they do not contradict existing road signs or traffic signals.
Only if you see it is necessary to do so.
explanation: Flaggers manage temporary hazards and always take priority in works zones.

text: How can you see if another vehicle is in your blind spot?
options: Lean back and forth whilst looking in the mirrors.
Look over your shoulder.
Set your side mirrors all the way to the outside.
This cannot be done, hence it's called a blind spot.
explanation: A quick shoulder check covers the mirror blind spots.

text: At a roundabout, you must yield to traffic approaching from your right and already in the roundabout.
options: True
False
explanation: Yield to circulating traffic and vehicles from your right.

text: How should you respond if you see a stationary vehicle on the side of the road?
options: Stop and offer assistance.
Slow down and use caution when passing by.
Notify the emergency services.
explanation: Reduce speed and pass with caution; stop only if it’s safe and necessary.

text: If you hurry, it is all right to overtake another vehicle as you're nearing the crest of a hill.
options: True
False
explanation: Never overtake near a blind crest; you cannot see oncoming traffic.

text: When overtaking, you may exceed the speed limit when you have to overtake a couple of vehicles at the same time.
options: True
False
explanation: You may not exceed the posted limit, even while overtaking.

text: If you come to a traffic light and the red light flashes, you must …
options: look out for a roadblock as the light shows you a police roadblock ahead.
stop and wait for the light to change to green before you move off.
stop and only move off if it is safe to do so and it is your turn.
explanation: A flashing red functions like a stop sign: stop, then proceed when safe.

text:
Which of the following vehicles are allowed on a freeway, if any?  (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. A tractor busy with maintenance work.
ii. A motorcycle with a engine cylinder capacity not exceeding 50cc.
iii. An animal-drawn vehicle.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Maintenance vehicles may be permitted; 50cc and animal-drawn vehicles are prohibited.

text: Which of the following always takes priority above the rest?
options: Road traffic signs.
Traffic signals (robots).
Instructions given by a traffic officer.
Road surface markings.
explanation: A lawful order from a traffic officer overrides signs, signals, and markings.

text: A safe following distance, at all speeds, for motorcycles and light motor vehicles is ...
options: 2 seconds.
3 seconds.
1 car length.
explanation: Two seconds is the standard minimum in good conditions.

text: A driver may ...
options: allow a passenger to help him or her steer the vehicle.
use hand signals on a freeway in an emergency.
allow a small child or pet to sit on their lap whilst driving.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Hand signals may be used in emergencies when indicators fail.

text: A driver may not …
options: leave a vehicle abandoned on a public road for 6 hours.
park a vehicle further than 1m away from the outside edge of the road.
let his only passenger sit where there is no seat belt.
explanation: All occupants must use an available, functional seat belt.

text: Where must you place the emergency warning triangle, if you experience a vehicle breakdown on the road?
options: Next to the vehicle.
At least 45m behind the vehicle.
On the roof of the vehicle.
At least 10m behind the vehicle.
explanation: Place the triangle about 45 m back to warn approaching traffic in time.

text: On a public road, the driver of a vehicle may not ...
options: cause any wheel of the vehicle to drag or spin on the roadway.
make use of chocks or shoes between any wheel of a moving vehicle.
use any vehicle, or move any vehicle, in a manner causing damage to the roadway.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: All listed behaviours are prohibited due to safety and road-damage risks.

text: Which of the following vehicles may be used on a freeway?
options: A pedal cycle.
A vehicle with a mass not exceeding 230kg, designed for the use of a person suffering from a physical disability.
A motorcycle with an engine capacity of 125cc.
None of the above.
explanation: 125 cc motorcycles are permitted; pedal cycles and very light mobility vehicles are not.

text: When may you talk on a mobile phone whilst driving?
options: When you hold the mobile phone between your shoulder and ear.
When you have to make an emergency call.
You are not allowed to talk on a mobile phone whilst driving, except through a hands-free kit.
explanation: Drivers may only talk using a hands-free kit; hand-held use is prohibited.

text: When you are driving on the freeway and you notice a vehicle in front of you wants to merge with the freeway from an on-ramp, you must …
options: Speed up to close the gap.
Maintain your speed.
Allow the vehicle to merge in front of you.
explanation: Always allow merging vehicles to join safely by adjusting your speed if necessary.

text: A motor vehicle which is designed for, or capable of, reaching a speed of ... km/h or more, must be equipped with a speedometer which is in good working order.
explanation: Any vehicle capable of 60 km/h or more must have a working speedometer.

text: When are you allowed to drive on a public road without a securely fitted and closed bonnet (engine cover) on your motor vehicle?
options: When you are in the process of repairing your vehicle.
When you have converted your vehicle into a race car.
Under no circumstances.
explanation: All vehicles must have securely fitted and closed bonnets when driven on public roads.

text: You are approaching an intersection and the traffic light turns amber (orange/yellow). You must …
options: Gear down and speed up to get across the intersection.
Reduce speed and stop behind the stop line, unless you cannot stop safely.
Hit the brakes hard and stop, even if you are going to stop over the stop line and pedestrian lines.
explanation: Amber means prepare to stop unless doing so would cause an accident.

text: Which of the following would disqualify you from obtaining a learner's licence? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)
options: Only (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct.
Only (iv) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Only those with an active licence suspension or disqualification are barred from obtaining a learner’s licence.

text: When are you expected to carry your original learner's licence?
options: Whenever you are the driver of a vehicle.
It is sufficient to carry a certified copy of your learner's licence when driving.
Only when you're driving and you're alone in the vehicle.
explanation: You must always carry your original learner’s licence while operating a vehicle.

text: When you are approaching a block pedestrian crossing, you must …
options: Ignore it and keep driving, if there are no pedestrians on the road.
Stop and wait for a crossing guard to signal you to continue.
Slow down, stop if necessary and wait for pedestrians to cross the road then proceed with caution.
explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians already on or approaching the crossing.

text: When approaching an intersection and you wish to turn left or right … (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (iii) is correct.
explanation: You should slow down, indicate early, and check for safe passage before turning.

text: Between sunrise and sunset you may drive on the shoulder of a single lane road when being overtaken by another vehicle, if it is safe to do so and you have a clear view of the road ahead for at least 150m.
options: True
False
explanation: This is allowed during daylight hours if safe and visible for at least 150 m.

text: You may not drive to the left of the outside edge line marking to overtake a slow-moving truck on a public road with traffic moving in both directions.
options: True
