False
This is permitted in an emergency.
explanation: Crossing left of the edge line is illegal on two-way roads.

text: You may not overtake a vehicle that has stopped at a pedestrian crossing.
options: True
False
explanation: Vehicles stopped at crossings often allow pedestrians to pass; overtaking them is unsafe.

text: The legal speed at which you may drive ...
options: Is different from town to town.
Depends on if the road is wet or dry.
Is determined by the appropriate signs next to the road.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Speed limits are set by the posted regulatory signs.

text: The sequence of the basic elements of defensive driving is ...
options: search, identify, predict, decide, execute.
predict, search, identify, decide, execute.
identify, predict, search, decide, execute.
explanation: The SIPDE process: Search, Identify, Predict, Decide, Execute.

text: Defensive driving means…
options: Defending yourself on the road.
Being an aggressive driver.
Maintaining a clear space around your vehicle at all times.
explanation: Maintain a safe space cushion and anticipate potential hazards.

text: Signal whenever … (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Always signal for lane changes, turns, or when stopping to warn others.

text: Turning signals (indicators), when in use, must be clearly visible …
options: From the back of the vehicle only.
From both the front and the back of the vehicle.
From the front, the back and the sides of the vehicle.
explanation: Signals must be visible from multiple angles for clear communication.

text: When being overtaken, you must ...
options: Maintain your current speed.
Slow down.
Speed up.
explanation: Maintain speed and position to help the other driver overtake safely.

text: What does 'one-way road' mean?
options: All vehicles on that roadway are travelling in the same direction only.
The road leads to one destination only.
The road has traffic travelling in both directions and each side has only one lane.
explanation: All vehicles move in the same direction on a one-way road.

text: You are allowed to drive against the traffic flow of a one-way road, provided you drive on the left-hand side of that road and your lane is clear of oncoming traffic.
options: True
False
explanation: Driving against traffic on a one-way street is strictly prohibited.

text: Do not enter or cross a road if …
options: you intend to turn right.
you are likely to cause a dangerous situation or obstruct traffic.
you have not first flashed your lights.
explanation: Enter only when it is safe and will not obstruct other vehicles.

text: You may overtake another vehicle on the left ...
options: when instructed to do so by a traffic officer.
on a public road in an urban area, where the roadway is wide enough for two or more lines of moving vehicles, if the other vehicle intends to turn right.
Both of the above are correct.
explanation: Left-side overtaking is only allowed when safe or under a traffic officer’s instruction.

text: Public transportation vehicles are allowed to …
options: hoot to attract passengers.
exceed the speed limit.
drive in the shoulder of the road.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Public transport drivers must obey all traffic laws like other motorists.

text: If you are driving in the far right-hand lane on a freeway and the car behind you flashes its lights, you should ...
options: Ignore it.
Signal and move across to the lane left of you, when it is safe to do so.
Accelerate.
Tap the brakes quickly to warn the car behind you to back down.
explanation: Move to the left when safe; the right lane is for overtaking.

text: If you are driving on a dual carriageway with more than one lane travelling in the same direction and you are driving faster than other vehicles, which lane should you use?
options: The left-hand lane.
The right-hand lane.
explanation: Use the right lane to overtake or when driving faster than other vehicles.

text: If you have changed lanes to the right to overtake another vehicle and you want to return to the left-hand lane, you must ...
options: Check the blind spot to the left and change lanes if it is safe to do so.
Check your rear-view mirror(s) and the blind spot to the left, signal (indicate) to the left, check the blind spot again and change lanes if it is safe to do so.
Signal (indicate) to the left and change lanes.
explanation: Perform mirror–signal–blind spot checks before returning to the left lane.

text:
Which of the following are not allowed on a freeway? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Pedestrians.
ii. Hand signals.
iii. Motor tricycles.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (iii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Pedestrians, hand signals, and certain vehicle types are prohibited on freeways.

text: A learner driver may transport passengers in a vehicle for remuneration, as long as he or she is supervised by someone with a driver's licence of the same code.
options: True
False
explanation: Learner drivers are not permitted to carry passengers for hire or reward.

text: Which of the following statements are applicable to pedestrians crossing a road at an intersection?
options: The 'red man' light signal shows pedestrians that they may not cross the road until the 'green man' light signal is displayed.
If the 'red man' light signal flashes, pedestrians who have not entered the roadway must wait until a 'green man' light signal is displayed.
Pedestrians who are already on the roadway when the 'red man' signal is displayed must cross as quickly as possible.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: All pedestrian signal rules listed apply at intersections.

text: You may not stop your vehicle within ... from any part of a roadway where the normal width thereof has been narrowed or constricted.
options: 1m
5m
6m
explanation: Vehicles must not stop within 6 metres of a narrowed section of roadway.

text:
A towed vehicle may not travel faster than 30km/h, unless ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. the tail lights are in working order.
ii. a solid tow-bar is used.
iii. the towed vehicle is a semi-trailer.
options: Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Higher than 30 km/h is allowed if a solid tow-bar is used or the towed unit is a semi-trailer.

text: When may you not overtake another vehicle?
options: On a one-way road.
If your view of the road ahead is restricted.
If there is only one lane for traffic travelling in both directions.
explanation: Never overtake when you do not have a clear view ahead.

text: You may ...
options: stop in the railway reserve at a level crossing.
stop opposite another vehicle, parked on a road less than 9m wide.
not stop within 9m of the approach side of a pedestrian crossing.
explanation: Stopping within 9 m of the approach side of a pedestrian crossing is prohibited.

text: Goods may be conveyed on a light or heavy motor vehicle, provided ...
options: the load is not wider than 2,5m.
the load projects no more than 300mm beyond the front of the vehicle.
Both of the above are correct.
explanation: Both width and front projection limits must be respected.

text: Which of the following statements are incorrect?
options: A hooter must be audible for at least 90m to a person of normal hearing.
A hooter may be used to greet people.
A hooter should be used only for safety purposes.
explanation: Using the hooter to greet is improper; it is for safety warnings.

text: Which statement is incorrect?
options: You may stop on the right-hand side of a one-way road.
You may stop on the right-hand side of a two-way road, only if you are facing the oncoming traffic.
You may not stop in a tunnel.
explanation: Stopping against the flow on a two-way road is illegal.

text: Unless otherwise indicated by a road sign, the general speed limit on rural roads is .....
options: 60km/h.
80km/h.
explanation: The rural (outside urban) default is 100 km/h for light vehicles unless posted otherwise.

text: At traffic circles, you must give way to ...
options: traffic which will cross their yield line before you.
traffic already in the circle, approaching from the right.
Both of the above are correct.
explanation: Give way to circulating traffic and to the right.

text:
Which of the following vehicles are defined as goods vehicles? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Truck-tractor
ii. Breakdown vehicle
iii. Converter dolly
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: All listed units fall under the goods vehicle category.

text: Gross Vehicle Mass (GVM) means ...
options: the combined mass of a vehicle and its load.
the mass of a vehicle without its load.
the mass of a vehicle's load only.
explanation: GVM is the maximum permissible mass of vehicle plus load.

text: Where must the licence disc of a motor vehicle be displayed?
options: Affixed to the lower left-hand corner on the inside of the windscreen.
Affixed to the upper left-hand corner on the inside of the windscreen.
Anywhere on the windscreen.
It does not have to be displayed and can be kept in the glove box of the vehicle.
explanation: Display the licence disc at the lower left of the inside windscreen.

text: A professional driver, driving a motor vehicle of a prescribed class, must have a/an …
options: Professional Driving Permit (PrDP).
Traffic Register Number (TRN).
International Driving Permit (IDP).
explanation: A PrDP is required for certain classes such as goods and passenger vehicles.

text: "LMV" means a light motor vehicle, of which the Tare or GVM shall not exceed ...
explanation: Light motor vehicles are up to 3 500 kg Tare or GVM.

text: What is required before a person can be legally trained to drive a vehicle on a public road?
options: A learner's licence.
A driver's licence.
The person must be at least 17 years old.
explanation: Training on public roads requires a valid learner’s licence.

text: When the holder of a driver's licence has changed their place of residence permanently, he or she must notify the registering authority of the new address within ...
options: 14 days.
21 days.
3 months.
12 months.
explanation: Address changes must be reported within 14 days.

text: How long is the grace period, after a vehicle's licence disc has expired, that it may still be operated on a public road?
options: 21 Days
1 Month
There is no such thing as a grace period.
explanation: A 21-day grace applies for relicensing; penalties may still accrue.

text: If the owner of a vehicle permits someone to use his or her vehicle, who would be legally responsible for traffic offences committed with such vehicle?
options: Owner
Driver
explanation: Owners can be held liable for offences committed with their vehicles.

text: You must turn on your vehicle's parking lights at night when it is parked ... or more from the nearest lit street lamp.
options: 6m
9m
explanation: Parking lights are required when parked 12 m or more from a lit street lamp.

text: The beam of a vehicle's headlamps must adequately illuminate the road ahead to at least ...
explanation: Headlamps must light up at least 100 m ahead.

text:
When should you dip the main beam of your vehicle's headlamps? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. For oncoming traffic.
ii. When following another vehicle.
iii. When you want to see better.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (iii) is correct.
explanation: Dip for oncoming traffic and when following another vehicle to avoid glare.

text: Which of the vehicle's lamps must be switched on when travelling at night through a city centre?
options: Parking lamps.
Headlamps - on dipped beam.
Headlamps - on main beam.
explanation: Use dipped beam in lit urban areas.

text: When you apply the foot brake, the stop lamps must emit a brighter red than the tail lamps and be visible in normal sunlight at a distance of ... to a person of normal eyesight.
explanation: Brake lights must be visible at 30 m in normal sunlight.

text: When a stop lamp is illuminated, this indicates that the vehicle ...
options: is decreasing speed and may stop.
is speeding up.
is going to change direction to the left or right.
explanation: Stop lamps warn following traffic of deceleration or stopping.

text: With how many number plates must light and heavy motor vehicles be fitted?
options: One fitted to the front and one fitted to the back of the vehicle.
Only one fitted to the back of the vehicle.
Only one fitted to the front of the vehicle.
explanation: Standard vehicles require plates at both front and rear.

text:
No vehicle may be driven on a public road while any fog lamp fitted is lit, except in certain conditions. Which are applicable? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Snow, fog or mist.
ii. Dust or smoke.
iii. Heavy rainstorm.
iv. Any time at night if you want to see better.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Fog lamps are for reduced-visibility conditions like fog/mist and dust/smoke, not general night driving.

text:
Which vehicles may be fitted with adjustable spot lamps and used on a public road? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Ambulances, fire-fighting vehicles and police vehicles.
ii. Medical practitioners' or veterinarians' vehicles, when used for professional duties.
iii. Breakdown vehicles, when used at the scene of an accident.
iv. Vehicles used for hunting and off-road purposes.
options: Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Emergency and certain professional/assistance vehicles may use adjustable spot lamps; off-road hunting use is excluded on public roads.

text:
You may not drive/ride a vehicle on a public road, unless ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. you have a full and clear view of the roadway ahead and to your right and left.
ii. such vehicle is fitted with a rear view mirror or mirrors for a clear rear view.
iii. such vehicle can reach a speed of at least 80km/h.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Clear forward view and mirrors are required; there is no 80 km/h minimum capability requirement.

text: What is the allowed maximum turning radius of a vehicle used on a public road, excluding that of a bus-train or rigid goods vehicle?
options: 9m
explanation: The maximum turning circle radius is 13,1 m (except specified classes).

text: Which of the following statements are incorrect?
options: On a freeway, vehicles must keep to the left and overtake to the right.
On a freeway, a driver may indicate intent to overtake a non-left-lane vehicle by flashing headlights.
On a freeway, you may drive on the shoulder to take the next off-ramp, only if traffic is congested and stationary on the freeway.
explanation: Driving on the shoulder to take an off-ramp is not permitted.

text: When about to pass oncoming traffic, a driver must …
options: ensure the vehicle does not encroach on the far right-hand side in a way that endangers oncoming traffic.
keep to the left of the roadway as far as possible, without driving off the edge.
flash headlights to make oncoming traffic aware.
explanation: Maintain safe lateral position; do not encroach into oncoming space.

text:
Which of the following vehicles are regarded as emergency vehicles? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. A fire-fighting vehicle (red identification lamps).
ii. An ambulance (red identification lamps).
iii. A vehicle driven by a traffic officer while carrying out duties (blue identification lamps).
iv. A vehicle driven by a person engaged in disaster management (green identification lamps).
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: All vehicles listed qualify as emergency vehicles when used for official duties.

text: The front window of a motor vehicle must have visible light transmittance through the windscreen of …
options: at least 30%.
at least 70%.
explanation: Windscreens must transmit at least 70% of visible light to ensure visibility.

text: How many windscreen wipers must light and heavy motor vehicles have? When in operation it must wipe the outside of the windscreen continuously, evenly and adequately.
options: At least one windscreen wiper, to clean the windscreen directly in front of the driver.
Two windscreen wipers, to clean the entire windscreen.
Three windscreen wipers. Two fitted to the front and one at the back.
explanation: Only one wiper is required, as long as it clears the driver’s view area adequately.

text: What is the function of the silencer of the exhaust?
options: Only to reduce noise from the engine.
To project exhaust gas from the engine through the silencer and reduce the sound produced.
To give your vehicle a nice sound, depending on the size of the silencer.
explanation: The silencer reduces exhaust noise and safely directs gases away from the vehicle.

text:
A vehicle may not be used on a public road ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. unless it is fitted with an efficient exhaust silencer.
ii. if the exhaust gas or smoke causes a nuisance or obstructs vision.
iii. if oil or other flammable liquid can drip onto the exhaust.
iv. if exhaust gas or smoke leaks into the cab or passenger area.
options: Only (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct.
Only (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: All listed conditions make a vehicle unfit for road use.

text: Which statement is true with regards to a vehicle's fuel tank?
options: The filling orifice of the fuel tank must be fitted with an effective cap at all times.
You may drive with a cloth in the filling orifice until you can replace the cap.
You only need a cap if you don’t want to spill fuel while driving.
explanation: A secure, fitted fuel cap is legally required for safety and emissions control.

text:
Displaying an emergency warning triangle shall not apply to a vehicle being stationary on the roadway of a public road ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. in a place where loading or unloading is authorized.
ii. in compliance with a road traffic sign or a traffic officer's direction.
iii. when stopped due to other traffic and the driver remains in the driver’s seat.
iv. when performing an official State or municipal function.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: All listed circumstances exempt a driver from placing a warning triangle.

text: What is the maximum allowed speed applicable to vehicles conveying passengers for reward?
options: 60km/h
80km/h
100km/h
120km/h
explanation: Passenger-carrying vehicles may not exceed 100 km/h unless otherwise indicated.

text: What speed limit applies to goods vehicles or combinations with a GVM or GCM greater than 9000kg?
options: 60km/h
80km/h
100km/h
explanation: Heavy goods vehicles over 9000 kg are limited to 80 km/h unless otherwise posted.

text: What is the permissible overall length of a motor vehicle, excluding articulated vehicles, combinations, buses or bus-trains?
explanation: Ordinary single vehicles may not exceed 12,5 metres in overall length.

text: What is the overall length allowed in the case of a combination of vehicles, consisting of a drawing vehicle and a semi-trailer?
explanation: A drawing vehicle with semi-trailer combination may be up to 18,5 metres long.

text:
Which of the following statements are correct regarding height? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. The overall height of a double-deck bus may not exceed 4,65m.
ii. The overall height of a goods vehicle may not exceed 4,3m.
iii. The maximum roof load height may not exceed half the vehicle’s height unless carrying a bicycle.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (iii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: All height limits stated are correct and enforceable.

text: When using a public road, what is the maximum width that any motor vehicle with a GVM of less than 12000kg may be?
explanation: Vehicles under 12 000 kg GVM may not exceed 2.5 metres in width.

text:
When transporting goods on a vehicle on a public road, which of the following statements are true? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Goods may obstruct rear view if marked with red flags.
ii. Goods may be transported on the roof if the load is not higher than half the car’s height.
iii. A bicycle on a roof is exempt from this height rule.
options: Only (ii) is correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Roof loads must not exceed half the vehicle height, except bicycles.

text:
If persons are being transported in a goods vehicle, that portion must be enclosed to a height of ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. at least 350mm above the surface upon which persons are seated.
ii. at least 500mm above the surface upon which persons are seated.
iii. at least 900mm above the surface upon which persons are standing.
iv. at least 1m above the surface upon which persons are standing.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (ii) and (iv) are correct.
explanation: Minimum enclosures: 350–500 mm for seated, 900 mm for standing passengers.

text:
Which of these vehicles would not be allowed on a public road? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. A vehicle carrying goods projecting more than 1,8m at the back.
ii. A light motor vehicle carrying a load under 2,5m width.
iii. A vehicle transporting goods projecting 350mm in front of the vehicle.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
explanation: Loads projecting over 1.8m rear or 350mm front are illegal.

text: If a light or heavy motor vehicle is fitted with brackets for the conveyance of goods, such brackets may not project more than ... beyond the widest part of the vehicle (excluding mirrors or indicators).
options: 150mm
300mm
450mm
explanation: Brackets may project a maximum of 150 mm from the widest part of the vehicle.

text:
Who may drive on or across the right-hand roadway of a divided public road? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Anyone overtaking slow traffic.
ii. A traffic officer on duty.
iii. Anyone turning right at an intersection.
iv. Anyone when instructed by a traffic officer.
options: Only (i) and (iv) are correct.
Only (ii), (iii) and (iv) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Only authorised drivers and those turning right or instructed may cross.

text: The driver or rider intending to pass a stationary bus must ...
options: be on the lookout for persons approaching or leaving such bus.
stop behind the bus and wait for it to move off.
accelerate quickly and drive past before it moves off.
explanation: Always anticipate pedestrians near stopped buses.

text: When changing lanes, the driver may not move from one lane into another unless he/she ...
options: can do so without obstructing or endangering other traffic.
has a clear view of the road ahead for at least 150m.
can speed up enough to take a gap between traffic.
explanation: Lane changes must never endanger or obstruct other road users.

text: How far must a vehicle's indicator lights be visible to a person of normal eyesight in daylight?
explanation: Indicators must be visible at 30 metres in daylight.

text: How many retro-reflectors must be fitted on the rear of a light or heavy motor vehicle and what colour must they be?
options: 1 (on outer corner); red
2 (one on each side); red
2 (one on each side); white
explanation: Two red reflectors must be fitted on the rear corners of motor vehicles.

text: It is compulsory to have yellow reflective material fitted to the sides and rear of ...
options: all vehicles transporting dangerous goods.
goods vehicles of which the GVM exceeds 3500kg.
goods vehicles of which the GVM exceeds 10000kg.
explanation: Goods vehicles over 10 000 kg GVM require yellow reflective markings.

text: Is it compulsory for a pedal cycle on a public road to have a white reflector in front and a red reflector at the rear?
options: Yes
No
explanation: Bicycles must have front white and rear red reflectors for night visibility.

text: Which of the following statements are correct regarding traffic circles?
options: At a roundabout, yield to vehicles already in the circle and those from your right.
At a mini circle, yield to vehicles already in the circle or reaching their yield line before you.
Both of the above are correct.
explanation: Both large and mini circle rules require yielding to vehicles in or to your right.

text:
You may stop your vehicle on a public road ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. in order to avoid an accident.
ii. in compliance with a road traffic sign.
iii. when a traffic officer instructs you.
iv. for any cause beyond the control of the driver.
options: Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Stopping is lawful in all listed unavoidable or instructed situations.

text:
Which of the following statements are true regarding stopping? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. You may not stop in a tunnel or on a bridge.
ii. You may not stop your vehicle within 6m from a tunnel or bridge.
iii. You may stop in a tunnel or on a bridge unless prohibited by a sign.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
Only (iii) is correct.
explanation: Stopping on or within 6 metres of tunnels or bridges is prohibited.

text: No person shall park a vehicle on the roadway outside an urban area or within ... of the edge of such roadway, except in a demarcated parking space.
options: 1m
6m
9m
explanation: Parking is prohibited within 1 metre of the edge outside urban areas.

text: In which instance may two or more passengers be carried inside or on a vehicle that is being towed faster than 30km/h?
options: In a caravan.
On a semi-trailer.
In a car.
In a minibus.
explanation: Passengers may only be towed in a semi-trailer under controlled conditions.

text: What is the speed limit for breakdown vehicles when towing another vehicle? Provided such vehicles do not exceed a lesser speed limit indicated by a road traffic sign.
options: 60km/h
80km/h
100km/h
120km/h
explanation: Breakdown vehicles towing another vehicle may not exceed 80 km/h unless a lower posted limit applies.

text: Unless permitted by an appropriate road traffic sign, you may not park your vehicle on the left-hand side of a roadway with the outside of any left-hand wheel thereof more than ... within the roadway.
options: 300mm
450mm
550mm
explanation: Your left wheels may not be more than 450 mm from the left edge when parking, unless signs permit otherwise.

text:
When are you allowed to park in a parking bay reserved for disabled persons’ vehicles? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. If you are a disabled person or the driver conveying disabled persons.
ii. If such vehicle is issued with a disabled sticker.
iii. If you are conveying elderly persons.
iv. If you have an emergency and there are no other bays available.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Use of disabled bays requires a qualifying person and a valid permit/sticker.

text:
Which of the following vehicles may stop or park anywhere on a public road, in the execution of duties and whilst displaying the applicable identification lamps? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Fire-fighting vehicles.
ii. Ambulances and medical response vehicles.
iii. A vehicle engaged in civil protection.
iv. A vehicle used for road construction or maintenance.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: All listed service vehicles may stop/park as necessary while on duty and displaying proper lamps.

text:
When is it compulsory to stop? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. In compliance with a road sign or a uniformed traffic officer’s direction.
ii. At the signal of a person herding animals across the road.
iii. When pedestrians are already crossing at a block pedestrian crossing.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: You must stop in all listed situations for safety and legal compliance.

text: Under adverse conditions (rain, slippery surface, poor visibility, or if followed too closely) the driver shall …
options: increase their following distance.
decrease their following distance.
put on the emergency warning lights.
explanation: Increasing following distance provides more reaction time in adverse conditions.

text:
Which of the following is allowed on a freeway? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Stopping/parking where reserved by an appropriate road sign.
ii. Being on foot in the shoulder under normal circumstances.
iii. Giving hand signals.
options: Only (i) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Stopping in a signed reserved area may be allowed; pedestrians and hand signals are not permitted on freeways.

text:
Under normal circumstances a combination of motor vehicles is restricted to ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. a drawing vehicle and a maximum of two trailers.
ii. a drawing vehicle and one other motor vehicle, which is not a trailer.
iii. a drawing vehicle and two other motor vehicles, which are not trailers.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
explanation: Permitted combinations include a drawing vehicle with up to two trailers, or one other motor vehicle.

text: A driver/rider involved in a motor vehicle accident must report such accident to a police station ...
options: within 24 hours.
within 48 hours.
only if someone was injured or if claiming from insurance.
explanation: Accidents must be reported to police within 24 hours.

text: If a person has been killed or injured and the accident completely obstructs the roadway, no vehicle may be moved unless ...
options: its position is clearly marked on the road or removal is authorised by a traffic officer.
the driver authorizes such removal.
a certified tow-truck arrives and removes the vehicle(s).
explanation: Positions must be marked or removal authorised to preserve evidence and safety.

text: The driver of a vehicle would be legally accused of driving under the influence when blood alcohol concentration is ... or more.
options: 0,02g per 100ml of blood
0,05g per 100ml of blood
0,2g per 100ml of blood
0,5g per 100ml of blood
explanation: The general legal limit is 0.05 g per 100 ml of blood.

text: A professional driver (with PrDP) would be legally accused of driving under the influence when blood alcohol concentration is ... or more.
options: 0,02g per 100ml of blood
0,05g per 100ml of blood
0,2g per 100ml of blood
0,5g per 100ml of blood
explanation: Professional drivers have a stricter limit of 0.02 g per 100 ml.

text:
Which rules apply to adjustable spotlights? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Vehicles of medical doctors, vets or breakdown contractors may have them.
ii. They must light up persons/vehicles at least 100 m ahead.
iii. They may be fitted to game-spotting vehicles used on public roads.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Only certain professional/emergency uses are allowed; other uses are restricted.

text:
Which of the following vehicles would be considered abandoned? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. Left causing danger/obstruction.
ii. Parked on a residential street and not moved for 48 hours.
iii. Left 24 hours in the same place on a public road outside an urban area.
iv. Left in a car park for more than 8 hours.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
Only (iii) and (iv) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Danger/obstruction and 24 hours outside urban areas meet abandonment criteria.

text:
It is a traffic offence when the driver/rider of a vehicle ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. stops when a person herding animals signals them to do so.
ii. spins the wheels when moving off.
iii. crosses a broken centre line to overtake.
iv. uses a vehicle without a cap on the fuel tank.
options: Only (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct.
Only (ii) and (iv) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Wheel-spinning and no fuel cap are offences; obeying a herder’s signal and crossing a broken line to overtake are allowed when safe.

text: When you are turning onto another road and pedestrians are already crossing that road, you must ...
options: sound your horn to warn them.
wait and allow them to cross.
continue driving since you have right of way.
explanation: Pedestrians already in the crossing have priority.

text: Before you reach the exit where you will be leaving the freeway, how should you position your vehicle?
options: In the shoulder of the road.
In the middle lane.
In the left-hand lane.
explanation: Move to the left-hand (exit) lane in good time before your off-ramp.

text: What is the ideal frequency for checking your rear-view mirror(s) whilst driving?
options: Every 5 to 8 seconds.
Every minute.
Only when changing direction, slowing or stopping.
explanation: Frequent mirror checks (about every 5–8 seconds) maintain situational awareness.

text: Pedestrians must cross a roadway only at a pedestrian crossing or intersection, or otherwise at a distance further than ... from such crossing or intersection.
options: 9m
explanation: If not using a crossing/intersection, pedestrians should be at least 50 m away.

text: You may not stop your vehicle alongside or opposite another vehicle on a road where the roadway is less than ... wide.
options: 6m
9m
explanation: Double-parking/obstructing is prohibited on narrow (under 9 m) roads.

text: Within an urban area, no person shall park on a public road which is less than ... wide, unless it is one-way and parking is permitted by sign.
options: 9m
explanation: On two-way urban roads under 5.5 m, parking on the roadway is generally prohibited.

text: When a vehicle is towing another on a public road and the distance between vehicles is ... or more, the towing rope must have a red flag.
options: 1m
explanation: At 1.8 m or more, the rope/bar must be clearly flagged for visibility.

text: The tread depth of a motor vehicle's tyres may not be less than ... mm.
explanation: The legal minimum tread depth is 1 mm (check across the whole tread).

text:
The distance it takes a vehicle to stop is ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. longer on a wet road than on a dry road.
ii. longer at higher speed.
iii. longer if the vehicle carries a load.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Wet roads, higher speed, and heavier loads all increase stopping distance.

text: If you are towing a vehicle with faulty brakes, you must ....
options: not drive faster than 30km/h.
use a tow-bar or draw-bar and not a rope.
not carry more than one passenger in the towed vehicle.
explanation: A rigid tow-bar/draw-bar is required when the towed vehicle’s brakes are faulty.

text:
When another vehicle is trying to overtake you, you must ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. keep as near to the left as is safe.
ii. not increase speed until it has passed.
iii. signal the other driver to use another lane.
iv. speed up to keep up with traffic.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (iv) is correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Keep left and maintain speed (or gently reduce if needed) to let the overtaker pass safely.

text: How long is a learner's licence valid for?
options: 12 months
18 months
24 months
explanation: Learner’s licences are valid for 24 months in South Africa.

text: When must you use an emergency warning triangle?
options: When you want to stop for a lunch break next to the road.
When your vehicle has broken down.
When parked outside a friend's house on the wrong side of the road.
explanation: Use the triangle to warn others when your vehicle is stationary due to breakdown/hazard.

text: Any load carried on a vehicle must …
options: be covered with sheeting.
not obscure the driver's view.
have red triangles or flags tied to it.
explanation: Loads may not obstruct the driver’s required fields of view.

text: Any SABS approved number plate(s) shall be affixed to a vehicle …
options: in such a manner that it is not easily detachable.
in an upright position or within 30 degrees of such position.
in such a manner that each letter and figure is clearly legible.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Plates must be secure, upright/near-upright, and clearly legible.

text: The number plate(s) of a vehicle should correspond with the ...
options: vehicle's licence disc.
driver's licence card.
province the vehicle is being used in.
explanation: Plates must match the registration/licence details on the vehicle’s licence disc.

text: Which statement is correct with regards to towing?
options: A tow rope may not be shorter than 3,5m.
The distance between two cars towing may not be more than 3,5m.
Passengers may travel in a car when it is towed faster than 30km/h.
explanation: When towing with a rope, the gap between vehicles may not exceed 3.5 m.

text:
Every light and heavy motor vehicle used on a public road, must be equipped with … which is/are in good working order. (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. a service brake
ii. a parking brake
iii. an emergency brake
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Vehicles must have a service brake, a parking brake, and an emergency/secondary system.

text:
Which statements are correct with regards to a vehicle's hooter? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. It may only be used for safety.
ii. It must be audible to a person of normal hearing from 90 m.
iii. Musical/tune hooters may not be used in private vehicles.
iv. The pitch may not change while in use.
options: Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (i) and (iv) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: All listed hooter requirements apply.

text: Unless permitted by a road traffic sign, how close to an intersection may you park your vehicle?
options: 1m
5m
6m
9m
explanation: Keep at least 5 m clear of intersections unless signs allow otherwise.

text: You may not park your vehicle upon or over the actuating mechanism of a traffic signal.
options: True
False
explanation: Parking on sensor loops obstructs signal operation and is prohibited.

text: The furthest that your vehicle's dim lights may hit the road surface ahead of the vehicle is ...
explanation: Dipped beams should illuminate the road up to about 45 m ahead.

text: What is the speed limit on a freeway for vehicles exceeding 9000kg? (Unless a lower posted limit applies.)
options: 80km/h
100km/h
120km/h
explanation: Heavy goods vehicles over 9 000 kg are limited to 80 km/h unless otherwise signed.

text: When a load on a vehicle projects more than 150mm to the side or more than 300mm to the rear, it must be marked by a red flag during the day of at least …
options: 300mm x 300mm
500mm x 500mm
1m x 1m
explanation: Daytime projection must be marked with a red 300×300 mm flag.

text: During daylight every number and letter of your vehicle's number plates should be clearly visible from a distance of … by a person of normal eyesight.
explanation: Plates must be legible from at least 20 m in daylight.

text: Your vehicle must be fitted with at least ... number plate lamp(s) at the rear, illuminating the number plate.
explanation: At least one rear lamp must illuminate the plate at night.

text: A light or heavy motor vehicle may not transport goods that project more than ... beyond the rear end of the vehicle.
options: 300mm
1m
explanation: Rear projection may not exceed 1.8 m.

text:
At night, when transporting a load projecting 150mm+ to the side or 300mm+ to the rear, the load should be marked by … (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. white reflectors on each front corner.
ii. red reflectors on each rear corner.
iii. yellow reflectors on the sides.
iv. red flags 300mm x 300mm front and back.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (iv) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Night marking uses front white and rear red reflectors on the load’s corners.

text: Upon a traffic officer's request, you must produce your driver's licence ... to avoid a fine.
options: Immediately
within 24 hours
within 21 days
explanation: You must produce your licence immediately on request.

text:
Where must the exhaust silencer of a vehicle be fitted? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. In the right-hand bottom corner at the rear of the vehicle.
ii. Where oil/flammables cannot drip onto it.
iii. So that exhaust gas/smoke does not leak into the cab or passenger area.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) and (iii) are correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Placement must prevent drips onto it and prevent fumes entering the cabin.

text:
The maximum height of a vehicle with any load on a public road is … (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. 4,3 m for goods vehicles.
ii. 4,65 m for double-deck buses.
iii. For a motorcar roof load: not more than half the car’s height, unless the load is a bicycle.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (iii) are correct.
Only (iii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: All listed height limits apply depending on vehicle and load type.

text: Under normal conditions, which brake should be applied to slow down or bring a vehicle to a standstill?
options: Service brake.
Parking brake.
Stopping brake.
explanation: Use the service (foot) brake to slow/stop while driving.

text: Under which circumstances, if any, may a motor vehicle without a valid motor vehicle licence be used on a public road?
options: When the vehicle is used on a quiet road.
When a special permit has been obtained.
When the driver is sure the vehicle is roadworthy.
Under no circumstances.
explanation: A special permit is required; otherwise it may not be used on public roads.

text: If you want to tow another vehicle with a tow rope on a freeway that has a minimum speed limit of 50km/h, at what speed should you drive?
options: 30km/h
50km/h
It is illegal to tow there at 50km/h with a rope, so you may not drive there.
explanation: Towing with a rope cannot meet the minimum-speed rule; such towing is prohibited there.

text:
Under which circumstances, if any, may a traffic sign be disregarded? (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. When ordered by a traffic officer.
ii. In an emergency.
iii. At night if the sign is temporary.
iv. Under no circumstances.
options: Only (i) is correct.
Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct.
Only (iv) is correct.
explanation: Only a traffic officer’s lawful instruction allows you to disregard a sign.

text: Which would be an example of defensive driving when you want to change lanes?
options: Check your mirrors, indicate and move across into the other lane.
Check mirrors and blind spot, indicate, re-check blind spot, and move only if safe.
Check if it is safe to do so and move across into the other lane.
explanation: Defensive changing requires mirror checks, blind-spot checks, signalling, and confirming it is still safe.

text: What does LMV mean?
options: Light Motor Vehicle
Legal Motor Vehicle
Large Motor Vehicle
Licenced Motor Vehicle
explanation: LMV stands for Light Motor Vehicle.

text: Driver hand signals: Right arm extended to the right, palm forward, indicates you intend to ...
options: stop.
slow down.
turn right.
turn left.
explanation: Arm extended to the right with palm forward signals a right turn.

text: When should you switch on the emergency warning lights of your vehicle?
options: When your vehicle is standing in a hazardous position on the road.
To thank someone for giving you a gap.
When stopping to pick up a passenger.
explanation: Hazard lights warn others of a stationary hazard or breakdown.

text: On a one-way road, you may overtake another vehicle when approaching a curve, the crest of a hill, or similar, provided it is safe and not prohibited by signs/markings.
options: True
False
explanation: On one-way roads you may pass if visibility and markings allow and it is safe.

text: You may overtake another vehicle across a solid white line between sunrise and sunset if you can see clearly for 150m ahead.
options: True
False
explanation: Crossing a solid white line to overtake is prohibited.

text: When overtaking another vehicle on the left-hand side, you may …
options: drive on the verge or shoulder for safety.
drive to the left of the left edge line marking whilst overtaking.
Both of the above are correct.
None of the above are correct.
explanation: You may not use the verge/shoulder or go left of the edge line to overtake.

text: Which statement is incorrect?
options: You may not park within 1,5 m on either side of a fire hydrant.
You may stop on a road to avoid an accident.
Neither of the above statements.
explanation: Both A and B are correct statements; therefore option C (neither) is the incorrect one.

text: A convoy may not operate from ... the night before until ... the morning after any weekend, long weekend or 25–26 December.
options: 5pm; 5am
6pm; 6am
8pm; 8am
explanation: Convoys are restricted between 18:00 and 06:00 over those periods.

text: What is the meaning of the word "intersection" (also known as a "junction")?
options: Any place where roads join or cross.
Only where roads cross at traffic lights/stop signs.
Only freeway on-ramps and off-ramps.
explanation: An intersection is any place where roads join or cross.

text: Unless otherwise indicated by a sign or signal, when do you have right of way?
options: When turning right at an intersection on a two-way road.
When turning left at an intersection on a two-way road, except when turning from a slipway.
When turning right and the only oncoming vehicle is turning the same way.
explanation: Left turns generally have priority on two-way roads unless signs/markings dictate otherwise or turning from a slipway.

text: When herding animals across a public road, a red warning flag during the day and a red warning light at night must be displayed ... ahead of and behind the herd.
explanation: Warning signals must be shown 150 m ahead of and behind the herd for visibility.

text: Except for overtaking, how far must an animal-drawn vehicle travel behind another animal-drawn vehicle on a public road?
options: Two car lengths.
At least 10m.
150m or more.
explanation: A following distance of at least 150 m reduces collision risk.

text: If you are turning right at an intersection ...
options: Oncoming traffic has right of way.
You have right of way.
You must wait for a flashing green arrow before you turn.
explanation: Yield to oncoming traffic when turning right unless otherwise directed.

text: When turning right at an intersection, which statement is correct?
options: You must pass the centre line of the road you are turning onto before you begin to turn.
You must head for the right-hand side of the road you are turning onto and then move across to the left-hand side.
When turning onto a one-way road you must always keep to the left before making the turn.
explanation: Positioning through the intersection before completing the turn prevents cutting corners.

text: You may not park ...
options: On a pavement.
Within 10m of an intersection.
Within 19m of the approach side of a pedestrian crossing.
explanation: Sidewalks are for pedestrians; parking on pavements is prohibited.

text: At a 4-way stop ...
options: You must stop and only move off if it is safe to do so.
You must stop and only move off when it is your turn, in the sequence that all vehicles have stopped.
You must stop, wait for 4 seconds and then move off.
explanation: Vehicles proceed in the order they stopped, when safe.

text: Unless otherwise indicated by a road traffic sign, the speed limit on freeways is 120km/h except for ...
options: Passenger vehicles conveying persons for reward.
Goods vehicles with a GVM of more than 9000kg.
Both of the above are correct
None of the above are correct.
explanation: Passenger-for-reward and heavy goods vehicles have lower limits.

text:
When you want to overtake another vehicle on the right-hand side, you must ... (SELECT THE CORRECT COMBINATION)

i. keep a safe distance from that vehicle.
ii. look out for approaching vehicles.
iii. not pass too close before moving back to the left-hand side.
options: Only (i) and (ii) are correct.
Only (ii) is correct.
All of the above are correct.
explanation: Safe gap, watch oncoming traffic, and don’t cut in too early.

text: What is the speed limit for buses and minibuses, transporting passengers at a fee, on all major roads and freeways? (Unless a lower posted limit applies.)
options: 60km/h
80km/h
100km/h
120km/h
explanation: Public transport buses/minibuses are limited to 100 km/h on major roads/freeways.

text: When may the driver of a motor vehicle use a handheld mobile phone whilst the vehicle is in motion?
options: When rushing a sick person to hospital.
In an emergency when calling the police.
Under no circumstances.
explanation: Handheld phone use while driving is prohibited.

text: A motor vehicle may not be used on a public road ...
options: Unless the electrical wiring and battery are properly installed and maintained without constituting a source of danger.
If the exhaust pipe is well maintained.
If the fuel tank is fitted with an effective cap.
explanation: Unsafe electrical systems make the vehicle illegal on public roads.

text: In which case are you permitted to drive only with the parking lights on?
options: When dusk is falling.
When it is raining.
At night in an urban area.
Never.
explanation: Parking lights alone are not sufficient while driving.

text: Which of the following vehicles are exempt from the no-parking rules?
options: Emergency vehicles, rescue vehicles, public service vehicles and traffic control vehicles, in the course of duty.
Delivery vehicles, motorhomes and vehicles towing caravans or long trailers.
Tour buses and delivery vehicles.
explanation: Emergency and official service vehicles may stop/park when performing duties.

text: When are you allowed to stop a vehicle on the sidewalk (pavement)?
options: When you need to pull off the road to answer your phone.
Any time after sunset, provided the parking lights are switched on.
When you stop to open or close a property gate.
explanation: Stopping briefly to operate a gate is allowed; otherwise sidewalks are off-limits.

text: Where are you not allowed to park?
options: Off the road, 4m from the outside edge of a roadway.
In a parking bay that is less than 4m from a traffic light.
Within 4m from an intersection.
explanation: Keep at least 4 m clear of intersections.

text: All vehicular collisions should be reported at a police station within 24 hours, even if no-one was injured in the collision.
options: True
False
explanation: Reporting within 24 hours is required.

text: Where a road is more than 10m wide it is permissible to stop alongside or opposite another vehicle.
options: True
False
explanation: On sufficiently wide roads (over 10 m), stopping alongside may be permitted if not otherwise prohibited.

text: Which action should you take when driving down a long, steep hill?
options: Select the neutral gear to save petrol.
Use the foot brake along with the handbrake.
Use the foot brake along with an appropriate lower gear.
Change up to a higher gear.
explanation: Use engine braking (lower gear) with controlled foot braking.

text: You must check the blind spot ...
options: Before changing direction.
After giving a signal.
When applying the brakes.
explanation: Always check blind spots prior to lane changes/turns.

text: What is the last thing you should do before turning right at an intersection?
options: Check your mirrors and blind spot to see that no other vehicles are overtaking you.
Look out for cross-traffic.
Signal your intention (indicate).
explanation: Final mirror and blind-spot check prevents conflicts with overtaking traffic.

text: Who is responsible for ensuring that all seatbelts are worn in a vehicle?
options: Each passenger in the vehicle.
The driver of the vehicle.
The parent of every child in the vehicle.
explanation: The driver is legally responsible for seatbelt compliance.

text: You may not drive a vehicle on a public road if the exhaust pipe …
options: Has a diameter larger than 40mm.
Is positioned where oil may drip onto it.
Is positioned so that it points to the side of the vehicle.
explanation: Risk of fire prohibits placement where oil/flammables may drip onto the exhaust.

text: You are allowed to drive with the fog lamps switched on only when visibility is poor due to ...
options: Snow, fog, smoke, dust and mist.
Mist, smoke, fog and heavy rain.
Fog, mist, smoke, dust and from sunset until sunrise.
explanation: Fog lamps are for severely reduced visibility conditions (not simply night driving).

text: In which of the following circumstances are you allowed to overtake another vehicle?
options: On approach to a pedestrian crossing, as long as the view ahead is clear.
Near the crest of a hill during daylight hours.
After going around a curve, when you have a clear view of the road ahead for more than 150m.
explanation: Only overtake when you have a long, clear view ahead and it is permitted.

text: When should a driver use hand signals?
options: When driving on a freeway to make your intentions more visible to other vehicles.
When your vehicle's indicator lights are not working and you need to change direction.
When the driver behind you is driving too close and might not see your vehicle's tail lights.
explanation: Hand signals are a backup if indicators fail.

text: Under which circumstances must parking lights be used?
options: When parked 10m from a street light at night.
When parked more than 12m from a street lamp after sunrise.
When parked outside a demarcated parking bay on a public road between sunset and sunrise.
explanation: Parking on a roadway after dark requires lights to warn other traffic.

text: When would it be sufficient to have only one red flag (300mm x 300mm) tied to a load that projects more than 300mm beyond the rear of the vehicle (during daytime)?
options: If the load is less than 600mm wide and does not project more than 150mm on either side of the vehicle.
If the load projects less than 1,8m beyond the rear of the vehicle.
If the load is tied together in a bundle.
explanation: A single rear flag suffices for a narrow load that doesn’t project >150 mm to either side.

text: The service brake (foot brake) must be able to bring a light motor vehicle, travelling at 35km/h on a dry road, to a complete stop within a maximum distance of ...
explanation: Regulations require stopping within 14 m at 35 km/h on a dry surface.

text: When you come to a roundabout, you ...
options: Have right of way over pedestrians crossing the road.
Must yield to vehicles approaching from your right-hand side.
Must stop and only move off when the roundabout is clear from left and right.
explanation: Yield to traffic approaching from the right and traffic already circulating.

text: When you encounter a set of robots (traffic lights) on the road and no disc or arrow is illuminated, it means that ...
options: The traffic lights are out of order and the intersection must be treated like a 4-way stop.
The traffic lights are no longer applicable and you can ignore them and continue driving.
Vehicles travelling on the major road have right of way and vehicles on the minor road must stop.
explanation: A dead signal is treated as a four-way stop for all directions.
